items.title: Canada time-zone change on 1 November: Outlook users in BC, Alberta and Manitoba must switch time zone and recheck meetings; an Exchange Online remediation cmdlet is due 28 October
items.officialTitle: Update to MC1510951: Canada 2026 time zone changes — Microsoft 365 impact and required admin actions
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states the clock change on 1 November 2026 (action required by 2026-11-01 07:00 UTC).
items.fingerprint: Published 26 October 2026 (19:32 UTC), after the morning read. On 1 November 2026 affected parts of British Columbia, Alberta and Manitoba (and the Northwest Territories and Northwestern Ontario with them) stay on UTC-07:00, UTC-06:00 and UTC-05:00. Confirmed impact: Outlook and Exchange Online calendars (existing events do not migrate; recurring meetings need review) and Teams Rooms on Windows showing time one hour behind until Edge/WebView2 is updated.
items.why: Not a security change, but a time-zone shift moves timestamps that sign-in, audit and detection queries correlate across; Teams Rooms devices one hour behind Windows also misreport meeting times.
items.action: Before 1 November make sure Windows devices in the affected regions have the October 2026 updates, update Edge and WebView2 on Teams Rooms on Windows, and plan to run the Exchange Online remediation cmdlet for non-recurring meetings once Microsoft releases it (target 28 October).

items.title: Edge 156 needs no new security baseline settings: the Edge 151 baseline stays the recommended configuration
items.officialTitle: Security Review for Microsoft Edge version 156
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft Security Baselines blog
items.fingerprint: Microsoft reviewed the new settings in Edge 156 and found no additional security settings that require enforcement; the Edge 151 security baseline remains the recommended configuration. Edge 153 to 156 introduced 8 new Computer and User settings, listed in a spreadsheet with the post. The Edge baseline follows the Extended Stable Channel.
items.why: Confirms the Edge baseline you deploy (151) is still current; no policy change is needed for Edge 156.
items.action: No action required by Microsoft. Keep the Edge 151 baseline; review the 8 new settings in the spreadsheet if you manage Edge policy beyond the baseline.

items.title: Network Watcher VNet flow logs can now be filtered before they are written (GA)
items.officialTitle: [Launched] Generally Available: Network Watcher VNet flow logs filtering
items.fingerprint: Azure Updates, 26 October 2026: filtering for Network Watcher virtual network flow logs is generally available. The feed entry gives the headline only; the filter options were not read in this pass.
items.why: Flow logs are a network log source for Sentinel and Traffic Analytics; a filter applied at source can silently drop the flows a detection relies on.
items.action: If you ingest VNet flow logs, decide who may set filters and check that any filter keeps the flows your network detections query.

items.title: Defender for Identity's 'operating system that will soon become unsupported' health alert now names Windows Server 2016; sensors keep reporting after its extended support ends
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Identity health alerts
items.publishedNote: Learn publish time 2026-10-25T17:38 UTC, recorded by the Learn mirror commit 8e12954 (upstream d8fe20c) together with the sensor v2 prerequisites page.
items.tier0Note: The sensor runs on domain controllers, AD FS and AD CS servers; a Windows Server 2016 DC is the host this alert now fires for.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised two Defender for Identity pages published 25 October 2026. The health alert 'Sensor running on an operating system that will soon become unsupported' previously said 'Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 reached end of support on October 10, 2023' and now says 'Windows Server 2016 is approaching extended end of support', pointing to a new Legacy operating systems section. The sensor v2 prerequisites page adds: 'After extended support ends, sensors on Windows Server 2016 continue to report to Defender for Identity and receive sensor updates. However, some functionality that relies on operating system capabilities might not be available.'
items.fingerprintBefore: The Defender for Identity sensor is running on an operating system that will soon become unsupported. Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 reached end of support on October 10, 2023.
items.why: Domain controllers still on Windows Server 2016 will start raising this health alert, and after 12 January 2027 parts of the sensor's detection may silently degrade on them while the sensor still shows as healthy and reporting.
items.action: List sensors by OS version in the Defender portal (Settings > Identities > Sensors), plan the upgrade of every Windows Server 2016 domain controller, AD FS and AD CS host before 12 January 2027, and treat the new health alert as a tracked work item rather than noise.
items.fingerprintAfter: The Defender for Identity sensor is running on an operating system that will soon become unsupported. Windows Server 2016 is approaching extended end of support.

items.title: Out-of-band security updates for .NET, ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7.4/7.6 and Visual Studio: the October Scan Cab was reissued on 25 October, so offline compliance scans run before then miss them
items.officialTitle: An updated version of the October 2026 Scan Cab is available
items.fingerprint: Published 26 October 2026 (02:10 UTC). Microsoft reissued the October 2026 Scan Cab (wsusscn2.cab) at 7:00 PM PDT on 25 October with metadata for out-of-band security updates: .NET 8.0 (KB5133964), .NET 9.0 (KB5133965), .NET 10.0 (KB5133966), .NET 11.0 RC3, Visual Studio 2019/2022/2026, PowerShell 7.6 and PowerShell LTS 7.4. The post lists CVE-2026-70197 (.NET remote code execution), CVE-2026-102870 (ASP.NET Core remote code execution), CVE-2026-114148 (ASP.NET Core elevation of privilege) and CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli decoder buffer overflow). Admins who deployed the Scan Cab before that time and use it to assess these products should reacquire and redeploy it.
items.why: Two remote code execution fixes outside Patch Tuesday land in runtimes that sit on web servers and admin hosts (ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7). An offline or WSUS-scan-cab compliance report taken with the earlier cab shows these hosts as compliant while they are not.
items.action: Redeploy the reissued wsusscn2.cab wherever offline scans are used, then find hosts running .NET 8/9/10, ASP.NET Core, PowerShell 7.4/7.6 or Visual Studio in Defender Vulnerability Management and patch internet-facing ASP.NET Core servers first.

items.title: CVE-2026-83862 (Windows Network Load Balancing RCE) re-scored from 9.8 to 8.8: attack vector is adjacent, not network
items.officialTitle: CVE-2026-83862 Windows Network Load Balancing Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.reference: no MC/RM post — MSRC Security Update Guide
items.publishedNote: 23 October 2026 is the date of this revision in the MSRC feed; the original publication date was not read this pass.
items.fingerprint: MSRC corrected the CVSS Attack Vector from Network (AV:N) to Adjacent (AV:A) because exploitation needs Layer 2 adjacency; the base score drops from 9.8 to 8.8. Microsoft calls it informational: hosts with the update installed need no further action.
items.why: The fix is unchanged, but exposure narrows to attackers on the same Layer 2 segment as an NLB host, which changes how you rank unpatched NLB clusters.
items.action: No new action from Microsoft. Keep patching NLB hosts; re-rank any exception that assumed a network-reachable 9.8.

items.title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyses the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply-chain compromise: credential theft through Python startup hooks
items.officialTitle: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft Security Blog
items.fingerprint: Published 23 October 2026, 18:12 UTC. Microsoft Threat Intelligence covers the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise: Python startup hooks, credential theft, remote code loading, detections and mitigations (summary from Microsoft's feed).
items.why: LiteLLM is a common gateway in front of AI model keys; a poisoned package version that steals credentials at Python start-up reaches every secret the host holds.
items.action: Search developer and build hosts for LiteLLM 1.107.0 and apply the detections and mitigations Microsoft lists in the post.

items.title: Entra Agent ID: an agent identity blueprint can now be disabled in all tenants at once, and Microsoft warns agents in other tenants may fail
items.officialTitle: Disable agent identities (Disable agent identities in your tenant)
items.fingerprint: The page adds a 'Disable in all tenants' option on the Disable menu under Entra ID > Agents > Agent blueprints, run as at least Agent ID Administrator, and a new consideration: disabling a multi-tenant blueprint in all tenants can make related agents in other tenants fail or lose functionality.
items.why: An Agent ID Administrator in the publisher tenant can now switch off a blueprint's agents everywhere it was installed; that is a kill switch for a compromised agent and an outage lever if misused.
items.action: Add disabling a blueprint in all tenants to the agent incident runbook and watch Agent ID Administrator assignments, since that role can now reach agents in other tenants.

items.publishedNote: Listed under 'Week of October 19, 2026' in Intune's what's new; the page was published to Learn on 23 October 2026 at 07:34 UTC.

items.title: Dataverse Basic User loses read access to custom connector definitions it does not own or was not shared, during October
items.officialTitle: Power Platform – Update for read access to custom connector definitions for Basic User role
items.fingerprint: In October 2026 users holding the Dataverse Basic User security role stop being able to read solution custom connector definitions unless they own the connector or it was explicitly shared with them; Microsoft says connector definitions and configuration details were readable without being intentionally shared.
items.why: Custom connector definitions carry endpoints, auth configuration and other details; until this change any Basic User in an environment could read them, so environments with sensitive connectors had a read path nobody granted on purpose.
items.action: Review which makers rely on reading connectors they do not own; where org-wide read is needed, create a custom role with organization-level Read on the Connector table instead of re-widening Basic User.

items.title: Insights Agent V2 reaches Frontier: admins can let agent owners see user ratings and comments, off by default
items.officialTitle: Insights Agent V2 Frontier
items.fingerprint: Insights Agent V2 is available in Frontier (public preview roll-out complete) and gives Microsoft 365 admins tenant-level visibility into agent adoption; feedback sharing with agent owners is off (No agents) by default and is set under Agents > Settings > Agent feedback sharing in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Submitter identities are not shown to agent owners.
items.why: Turning sharing on sends users' ratings, comments and feedback themes to whoever owns an agent, including makers outside IT; the default is off, so the risk only arrives with an admin decision.
items.action: Leave Agent feedback sharing at No agents until owners of shared agents are known; if enabled, prefer Selected agents.

items.title: Defender XDR permission Emails associated with alerts now also opens email content for two URL-click alerts
items.officialTitle: Custom permissions in Microsoft Defender XDR Unified role-based access control (RBAC)
items.fingerprint: Learn page published 22 Oct 2026 07:38 UTC: the permission Email & collaboration content: Emails associated with alerts was described as covering the alerts Email reported by user as malware or phish and Email reported by user as junk; it now also covers A potentially malicious URL click was detected and A user clicked through to a potentially malicious URL.
items.why: Holders of an existing custom role can now view and download the email content behind two more alert types; no role was re-assigned, so nothing in the role audit trail marks the moment their reach grew.
items.action: List the Defender XDR custom roles that grant Emails associated with alerts and confirm every holder should see message content for URL-click alerts.

items.title: Microsoft names Storm-1849 Crystal Typhoon (China) and Storm-0156 Viridian Vortex (Pakistan), and attributes Sunglow Blizzard to Russia
items.officialTitle: How Microsoft names threat actors
items.fingerprint: Learn page published 22 Oct 2026 07:38 UTC: the Storm-0156 and Storm-1849 rows are gone; Crystal Typhoon (China) lists Storm-1849 and UAT4356 as previous names, Viridian Vortex (Pakistan) lists Storm-0156, MYTHIC LEOPARD, APT36, SideCopy and Transparent Tribe, and Sunglow Blizzard (DEV-0665) gains the origin Russia.
items.why: Detection rules, watchlists and TI tags keyed on Storm-0156 or Storm-1849 stop matching Microsoft's new advisories and Defender threat analytics under the new names.
items.action: Add Crystal Typhoon and Viridian Vortex as aliases wherever Storm-1849 or Storm-0156 appear in hunting queries, TI tagging and reports.

items.title: Work IQ can ground Copilot on business-application data; admin controls in Microsoft 365 and Power Platform admin centers reach public preview by 17 November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Copilot - Admin controls to manage Business Applications in Work IQ
items.fingerprint: Public preview by 17 November 2026 of admin controls that let business-applications (Dataverse/Power Platform) data ground Work IQ experiences next to Microsoft 365 data. Three layers: AI admins in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings and the Work IQ MCP under Agents > Tools; platform admins in PPAC choose which environments Work IQ reasons over and acts on; makers pick the apps and data inside an enabled environment. Microsoft states enabling it does not replace or expand existing user, agent, application or data permissions.

items.action: Before enabling the preview, review permissions on the Dataverse environments in scope, decide which environments Work IQ may reason over and act on, and record which admin layer owns each decision.

items.title: Microsoft 365 apps admin center can remotely repair Office installations that fall behind on updates (Update Repair in Inventory)
items.officialTitle: Microsoft 365 apps: Introducing Update Repair in Inventory
items.fingerprint: Public preview rolling out mid to late October 2026, GA mid to late November 2026. In the Microsoft 365 apps admin center (Inventory must be enabled) admins see Windows devices whose Microsoft 365 apps are out of date or failing to update and can start Online Repair remotely; repair closes open Office apps and reinstalls on the device's configured channel. Repair needs build 16.0.20326.20000 or later.
items.why: Out-of-date Office builds are an unpatched-vulnerability population; this gives a remote fix for devices stuck on old builds, and a new remote action an admin can trigger against endpoints.
items.action: Enable Inventory in config.office.com if it is off, compare its list of out-of-date devices with your vulnerability-management data, and restrict who holds the Office Apps Admin role since it can now trigger reinstalls.

items.title: Cross-tenant calendar sharing on Cross-Tenant Access Policy slips to 30 October; EWS-based Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing keep breaking as EWS is disabled
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
items.deadlineNote: Updated 20 October 2026: Calendar Sharing via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy completes rolling out by 30 October 2026 (previously 15 October). EWS disablement began 1 October 2026; the EWSEnabled extension lasts until the final shutdown on 1 April 2027.
items.fingerprint: EWS deprecation began 1 October 2026 and is being rolled out gradually. Cross-tenant Free/Busy and MailTips via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy were due by 15 September; Calendar Sharing moved on 20 October from 15 October to 30 October 2026 (end-October). Government clouds paused. Tenants with Organization Relationships or Sharing Policies to other Microsoft 365 tenants are affected; hybrid and on-premises are out of scope. Setting EWSEnabled to True keeps EWS until the final shutdown on 1 April 2027.
items.why: Partners lose sight of free/busy and shared calendars as EWS reaches the tenant; the usual workaround — re-enabling EWS — keeps a legacy, high-privilege API surface open for another five months.
items.action: Run Get-OrganizationRelationship and Get-SharingPolicy as the post shows; migrate Free/Busy and MailTips now and Calendar Sharing after 30 October, and if you set EWSEnabled to True, record it as a time-boxed exception ending 1 April 2027.
items.changeNote: Calendar Sharing completion moved at source on 20 October 2026: 2026-10-15 → 2026-10-30.

items.title: Cross-tenant delegated administration in Defender is generally available, extends to Sentinel and runs on Entra Tenant Governance relationships
items.officialTitle: Expanded cross-tenant delegated access in Microsoft Defender is generally available
items.tier0Note: Touches a tier-0 control: a cross-tenant delegated-access path to Defender and Sentinel.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Sentinel Blog, 20 October 2026: GA of cross-tenant delegated administration in Microsoft Defender on the Entra Tenant Governance relationship model, extended to Sentinel resources. A three-step consent handshake (governed tenant invites, governing tenant sends a request with an access template of security groups and Entra role assignments, governed tenant approves and assigns roles and scopes). Governing-tenant security groups appear in the governed tenant as remote tenant groups that receive Defender unified RBAC roles (custom roles included) or, for Sentinel, Defender unified RBAC or Azure RBAC; the governing tenant manages group membership. Aimed at MSSPs (non-CSP) and multitenant organisations. The Learn page Governance relationships was revised on 21 October 2026 (mirror commit a222810): Sentinel permissions for remote tenant groups can now be granted as Option 1 through Defender unified RBAC (Setup & Configuration > Permissions > Roles, choosing data collections) or Option 2 through Azure RBAC on a resource group.
items.why: Group membership in another tenant now decides who can act in your Defender and Sentinel: a compromised account or a sloppy group in the partner's tenant inherits that access without any change in yours.
items.action: Inventory governance relationships and remote tenant groups in Defender, scope each to a custom unified RBAC role with the least permissions, alert on new relationship approvals, and agree with the partner how membership of their groups is reviewed.

items.title: Sentinel Unified Data Management (public preview) puts connector health, table ingestion and spikes or drops on one page in the Defender portal
items.officialTitle: Manage all your Microsoft Sentinel data in one place with Unified Data Management (Public Preview)
items.fingerprint: Public preview announced 20 October 2026 under Setup & configuration > Data & connectors in the Defender portal, with Overview, Connectors and Tables tabs: daily ingestion by Analytics and Data Lake tier, connectors with credential errors, ingestion failures or outages and their last successful ingestion, tables with unexpected spikes or drops, top ingesting tables, and per-table schema, transformations and retention.
items.why: A silent connector is a silent detection: one view of connectors with failures and tables whose volume dropped is the quickest way to notice that an analytics rule has stopped seeing data.
items.action: Open Data & connectors > Overview, clear the connectors flagged as needing attention, and add a weekly check of tables with ingestion drops to the SOC health routine.

items.title: KMS Hardware-Secured: KMS hosts will have to prove their hardware with TPM attestation before activating clients, mandatory from the next Windows Server LTSC
items.officialTitle: Strengthening Key Management Service - (KMS) with Hardware-Based Trust
items.fingerprint: Windows IT Pro Blog, 20 October 2026: KMS Hardware-Secured uses TPM-based attestation so a KMS host proves it runs on trusted, untampered hardware before it activates Windows devices; Microsoft cites fake or cloned KMS servers. Windows Server 2025 shows readiness messages (slmgr /dlv and Key Management Service event log warnings) from August 2026; with the next Windows Server LTSC release TPM attestation becomes mandatory. Check support with Get-TpmSupportedFeature -FeatureList "Key Attestation". Guidance for virtual KMS hosts is promised later.
items.why: Rogue KMS hosts are a known way to activate untrusted machines inside a network; KMS hosts on hardware without TPM attestation will stop qualifying with the next LTSC.
items.action: Inventory KMS hosts (DNS _vlmcs SRV records), check slmgr /dlv and the Key Management Service event log for readiness warnings, and run the Key Attestation check on physical hosts.

items.title: Application Gateway terminates TLS without holding the private key: keyless TLS with Key Vault Managed HSM is generally available
items.officialTitle: Generally Available: Keyless TLS on Application Gateway with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Azure update only
items.fingerprint: Azure update of 20 October 2026: Application Gateway supports keyless TLS termination using certificates whose private keys stay in Azure Key Vault Managed HSM; each handshake signature is performed inside the HSM and the key is never exported to the gateway.
items.why: Removes the exportable TLS private key from the gateway, so a gateway configuration compromise no longer yields the key.
items.action: For public endpoints whose keys must stay in an HSM, evaluate moving Application Gateway listeners to Managed HSM-backed keyless TLS.

items.title: Azure Front Door Premium WAF custom rules can match on Azure service tags (generally available)
items.officialTitle: Generally Available: Service tag match condition for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Azure update only
items.fingerprint: Azure update of 20 October 2026: GA of a service tag match condition for WAF custom rules on Azure Front Door Premium; service tags are Microsoft-maintained groups of IP prefixes used by Azure services.
items.why: Allow or block rules keyed to Azure service IP ranges no longer need hand-maintained IP lists that drift out of date.
items.action: Replace hand-maintained Azure IP allow-lists in Front Door WAF custom rules with service tag conditions where they exist.

items.title: Route tables can suppress system peering routes on a subnet (Disable VNet peering route, public preview)

items.title: CVE-2026-102204 (WSL elevation of privilege) now names Windows Subsystem for Linux as the affected product; update WSL to the latest version
items.officialTitle: CVE-2026-102204 Windows Subsystem for Linux Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
items.fingerprint: MSRC revision of 20 October 2026: 'Updated CVE to reflect that this vulnerability is in the Windows Subsystem for Linux product. Microsoft recommends that customer using this product should install the latest version to be protected.' The same day six other CVEs (CVE-2026-96913, -70074, -83839, -83782, -70337, -62913) changed only an acknowledgement, which Microsoft calls informational.

(1) Cloud security plan management in the Defender portal for Azure commercial: connect subscriptions and management groups, enable plans globally or per scope, estimate costs in Defender Workload Units, 30-day trials; once plan management moves, configuration is managed in the Defender portal and becomes view-only in the Azure portal, and migrated subscriptions use DWU billing. items.title: Entra docs: an app Microsoft disabled cannot be re-enabled by any tenant admin, even in its home tenant; only a support case can reverse it
items.officialTitle: Protect against consent phishing — If you believe Microsoft disabled an application in error
items.tier0Note: Touches a tier-0 control: an app consent path.
items.fingerprint: New section added 20 October 2026: tenant administrators can't reverse Microsoft disablement by setting the service principal's accountEnabled to true or reactivating the app registration (isDisabled=false), and this applies to the application's home tenant too. A publisher must have a home-tenant admin open a support request with the client ID, home tenant ID, disabledByMicrosoftStatus value and findings; a support request does not guarantee reactivation. Application properties page updated the same way.
items.why: A Microsoft-disabled app is a strong signal of consent phishing or abuse; knowing that no admin can flip it back means an alert on disabledByMicrosoftStatus is final, and a request to 're-enable it' is itself suspicious.
items.action: Hunt for service principals with a non-null disabledByMicrosoftStatus, investigate their past consents and sign-ins, and route any re-enable request through the support process the page names.

items.title: Sentinel SAP BTP solution adds a rule that flags interactive use of custom apps with open high or critical vulnerabilities

Preview.
items.why: A detection that ties a known-vulnerable custom app to someone actually using it, which is the case worth paging on.
items.action: If you run the SAP BTP solution, update it from Content hub and enable the rule; it needs the SAP Application Vulnerability Report findings ingested.

items.title: Global Secure Access client for Windows 2.34.222 adds web sign-in for Windows and Conditional Access sign-in frequency for Private Access apps
items.officialTitle: Global Secure Access client for Windows release notes — Version 2.34.222
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no release date for 2.34.222. The section was added in MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs commit 692bdb5 (15:34 UTC, 19 October 2026), merged to the live branch at 17:36 UTC and confirmed on the published page through the Microsoft Learn MCP server; 19 October is the day it appeared, not a release date.
items.fingerprint: New section 'Version 2.34.222' on the Global Secure Access Windows client release notes. Functional changes: support for Web sign-in for Windows; with Private Access enabled and the device off the corporate network, Windows Firewall does not activate the domain profile; Conditional Access sign-in frequency for Private Access applications, rolling out gradually; the Prefer local network option bypasses only connections to IP addresses in common private network ranges. Other changes: UDP tunneling, memory, telemetry, accessibility and bug fixes.
items.why: Sign-in frequency on Private Access apps makes a re-authentication policy enforceable for on-premises applications reached through the client, and the narrowed Prefer local network bypass closes a path where traffic to non-private addresses skipped the tunnel. Both change what a Private Access sign-in log shows.
items.action: Pilot 2.34.222 on a test ring, check that sign-in frequency on a Private Access app prompts as configured, and confirm devices off the corporate network no longer report the domain firewall profile; from November 2026 Windows Update upgrades the client automatically unless you opted out.

items.title: Quick machine recovery reaches Windows Server 2025 with the October 2026 security update, switched off by default
items.officialTitle: Quick machine recovery is now supported on Windows Server 2025
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 19 October 2026 (14:21 UTC). With the October 2026 Windows security update, Quick machine recovery is available on Windows Server 2025: after a critical boot failure the server can use WinRE to search Windows Update for an applicable remediation. It is disabled by default and enabled through Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery); automatic remediation can be configured to run without user interaction. No immediate action is required.
items.why: Enabled, the feature lets a server that cannot boot fetch and apply a remediation from Windows Update before the OS starts, which is a change-control and evidence question on domain controllers and other tier-0 servers; nothing changes until the policy is turned on.
items.action: Decide per server class whether quick machine recovery may be enabled; if you enable it, exclude or explicitly approve domain controllers and record the Group Policy setting in your baseline. Confirm in your own tenant.

items.title: Cross-tenant access: Microsoft now states that changing the default redemption order needs an Entra ID P1 licence on the tenant you configure
items.officialTitle: Overview: Cross-tenant access with Microsoft Entra External ID
items.publishedNote: Read from MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs commit d232317 (15:00 UTC, 13 October 2026) and confirmed on the published Learn page through the Microsoft Learn MCP server at 21:20 Warsaw.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised 'Overview: Cross-tenant access with Microsoft Entra External ID' on 13 October 2026. It previously said: 'To configure trust settings or apply access settings to specific users, groups, or applications, you need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.' It now says: 'To configure trust settings, change the default redemption order, or apply access settings to specific users, groups, or applications, you need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.'
items.fingerprintBefore: To configure trust settings or apply access settings to specific users, groups, or applications, you need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.

items.title: Registration campaign: passkey nudges now also appear on interactive SSO sign-ins that satisfy MFA, and the passkey profile is evaluated first
items.officialTitle: Run a registration campaign to set up Microsoft Authenticator
items.publishedNote: Read from the MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs live-branch merge 7d26185 (17:39 UTC, 12 October 2026); the Microsoft Learn search index still served the earlier text at 21:38 Warsaw, so the published page may lag by hours.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised 'Run a registration campaign to set up Microsoft Authenticator' on 12 October 2026. It previously said: 'The nudge doesn't trigger if the user is already signed in with SSO.' It now says: 'Yes, during interactive sign-ins that satisfy multifactor authentication (MFA), provided users meet the registration campaign's other eligibility requirements. Silent SSO events that occur without user interaction, such as refresh token redemption, don't display nudges.'
items.fingerprintBefore: The nudge doesn't trigger if the user is already signed in with SSO.
items.why: More users will see a passkey registration prompt than the old text promised, and AAGUID-restricted or attestation-enforced profiles stop the nudge everywhere after one eligible passkey; helpdesk and phishing-awareness messaging should match what users will actually see.
items.action: Tell the helpdesk that registration nudges can appear on interactive SSO sign-ins; check which passkey profile each campaign target group is scoped to, since that now decides whether the nudge is per platform or tenant-wide.

items.title: Attested passkeys in Authenticator: Android users can now register them through a cross-device flow; iOS stays in-app only

items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised 'Enable passkeys in Authenticator' on 12 October 2026. It previously said: 'Users can only register attested passkeys directly in the Authenticator app. Cross-device registration flows don't support registration of attested passkeys.' It now says: 'On iOS, users can only register attested passkeys directly in the Authenticator app. On Android, users can register attested passkeys directly in the Authenticator app and by using a cross-device registration flow.'
items.fingerprintBefore: Users can only register attested passkeys directly in the Authenticator app. Cross-device registration flows don't support registration of attested passkeys.
items.why: With attestation enforced, a passkey for an Android Authenticator can now be registered from a laptop session over the cross-device (hybrid, Bluetooth plus cable.ua5v.com) flow, so the registering session is no longer always on the phone itself.
items.action: Expect Android passkey registrations whose sign-in originates on a desktop; review 'User registered security info' audit events with a Microsoft Authenticator AAGUID against the registering session's device and IP, and keep cable.ua5v.com reachable where cross-device registration is wanted.

items.title: File Integrity Monitoring in Defender for Servers: enabling or changing it now needs Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that holds the Log Analytics workspace
items.officialTitle: Enable File Integrity Monitoring
items.publishedNote: Dated from the published Learn page: updatedAt 2026-10-11 22:36 UTC (front matter ms.date moved from 3 July to 6 October 2026), read from the Learn mirror commit 46ea1f7 and re-read through the Microsoft Learn MCP server on 12 October.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised the prerequisites of 'Enable File Integrity Monitoring' (Defender for Servers Plan 2, powered by Defender for Endpoint) on the published page on 11 October 2026. It previously said: 'Have Workspace owner and Security admin permissions to enable and disable File Integrity Monitoring. Security reader permissions can view results.' It now says: 'To enable, disable, or change the File Integrity Monitoring configuration, have the Security Admin and Owner roles on the subscription that contains the Log Analytics workspace' and 'The Security Reader role can view results.' items.title: A Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy, Require risk remediation for high-risk users, starts in report-only mode and switches On the week of 28 October
items.officialTitle: Microsoft-managed CA policy coming to your tenant: Require risk remediation for high-risk users
items.publishedNote: Dated from the Message Center page on mc.merill.net (published 21 September 2026). The post is not in DeltaPulse and entered the mirror index only in this run, which is why no earlier brief carried it.
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states 'Week of October 28, 2026: End of evaluation period - policy will be enforced'; the date is the start of that week as stated.
items.fingerprint: Message Center MC1476122, published 21 September 2026, Microsoft Entra, for tenants with Microsoft Entra ID P2: Microsoft creates a Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users' and a new security group. Week of 28 September 2026: 'The Microsoft-managed CA policy will be created in report-only mode.' Week of 28 October 2026: 'End of evaluation period - policy will be enforced.' When On, users identified as high user risk are prompted to self-remediate through Entra ID Protection, and risk is cleared after successful remediation. 'No existing Conditional Access settings or exclusions (such as break-glass accounts) will be altered.' Admins can review the policy, set it to Off before the evaluation ends, or customise it, for example by excluding emergency access accounts.
items.why: From the week of 28 October a policy the tenant did not write starts deciding sign-ins for high-risk users. Emergency access accounts are not excluded automatically, and a high-risk user without a registered MFA method cannot self-remediate and is blocked, which the help desk will see before the SOC does.
items.action: Find the Microsoft-managed policy in Conditional Access now (report-only since the week of 28 September), read its report-only results in the sign-in logs, exclude break-glass accounts, confirm the users it would touch can complete MFA, and decide before 28 October whether it turns On or is set to Off.
items.backfillNote: Published 21 September; the post is absent from DeltaPulse and appeared in the mc.merill.net index read by collect_mc.py for the first time on 12 October.

items.title: Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider extension for Arc-enabled Kubernetes retires on 9 October 2027; the Secret Store extension replaces it
items.officialTitle: Retirement: Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters
items.publishedNote: Dated from the Azure updates feed entry, 9 October 2026 20:27 UTC.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's Azure updates feed, 9 October 2026: 'The Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes will be retired on October 9, 2027. Customers currently using the extension should plan to migrate to the Azure Key Vault Secret Store Extension before the retirement date.' Microsoft's migration guide says the two extensions are not supported side by side in one cluster, that the Secret Store extension authenticates with workload identity federation so 'no long-lived credentials are stored on the cluster', that it supports Linux only and no sovereign cloud, and that it writes Key Vault contents into native Kubernetes Secret objects.
items.why: The retiring extension mounts Key Vault secrets through a CSI driver with a service principal credential held on the cluster; its replacement drops that stored credential and instead keeps a copy of every secret in the Kubernetes secret store. The credential risk goes down and the exposure of the secrets to cluster RBAC, audit and etcd encryption goes up, so the migration is a security review and not a version bump.
items.action: List Arc-enabled clusters carrying extension type microsoft.azurekeyvaultsecretsprovider (az k8s-extension list), plan the switch-over window Microsoft describes, confirm encryption at rest and RBAC on Kubernetes Secrets before migrating, and revoke the old service principal on the vault when the migration is done. Clusters in Azure Government or Azure China have no replacement stated yet.
items.backfillNote: Published at 20:27 UTC on 9 October and inside the period yesterday; the feed entry was read on 10 October and not carried as an item. Added in the 11 October morning pass.

items.title: Entra Health Monitoring documents two new alert scenarios for AI agents: Agent ID interactive sign-ins and Agent ID autonomous sign-ins (preview)
items.officialTitle: How to investigate Agent ID autonomous sign-ins
items.fingerprint: Two new articles and two table-of-contents entries. The autonomous scenario counts a failure when the sign-in has a nonzero status.errorCode, agentType agenticAppInstance and an agentSubjectType other than agentIDuser, and is investigated in Service principal sign-ins. The interactive scenario selects agentSubjectType agentIDuser and 'uses agent-user activity in the User sign-ins (non-interactive) logs. Filtering only User sign-ins (interactive) or isInteractive = true can miss the failures relevant to this scenario.' The alert named on the page is 'Large increase in Agent ID interactive sign-in failures'. Reports Reader is the least privileged role to view the signals, alerts and sign-in logs; alerts need a non-trial Entra P1 or P2 licence and at least 100 monthly active users. Health scenario monitoring and alerts are in preview.
items.why: Agent identities are a new kind of non-human sign-in, and this is the first Microsoft-built signal that tells a SOC when their failure volume jumps. The pages also settle where to look: an agent acting with user context is in the non-interactive user log, not the interactive one, and an agent acting as itself is in the service principal log.
items.action: If the tenant runs Entra agent identities, open Health Monitoring, find the two Agent ID scenarios under All scenarios and add them to the alert notification configuration; in sign-in log queries for agents, filter on agent.agentSubjectType and agent.agentType rather than on isInteractive.

Unchanged: 'Users with existing MSA role assignments aren't impacted at this time. However, these users need to transition to a Work or School account (WSA) in a future phase.'
items.why: Enterprise Agreement roles are assigned outside Entra roles and Azure RBAC. Microsoft's page says an Enterprise administrator can 'Create new subscriptions under active enrollment accounts' and an Account owner can 'Manage subscription role assignments'. A personal Microsoft account holding one of them signs in outside the tenant's Conditional Access and sign-in logs (inferred). items.deadlineNote: Two expiry dates: 17 May 2027 for Windows 10 Enterprise 2019 LTSC, Windows Server 2019 and Windows Server 2016; 19 June 2027 for the other in-support versions.
items.title: Windows Update trust certificates expire on 17 May and 19 June 2027: a device below the July 2026 security update, or below September 2025 on Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025, stops receiving updates
items.officialTitle: Prepare for Windows Update certificate rotation in 2027
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 8 October 2026, category Stay informed: 'Certificates that help devices establish trusted connections to Windows Update will expire on May 17, 2027, and June 19, 2027. Devices must contain the replacement certificates to continue connecting to Windows Update and receiving updates after the applicable expiration date.' Windows 11 25H2 and later: no action. Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025: the September 2025 security update or later before 19 June 2027. Other in-support Windows 11, Windows Server 2022 and in-support Windows 10: the July 2026 security update or later before 19 June 2027. Windows 10 Enterprise 2019 LTSC, Windows Server 2019 and Windows Server 2016: the July 2026 security update or later before 17 May 2027. 'This change does not apply to devices receiving updates from Windows Server Update Services (WSUS).' Confirm in your own tenant.

Microsoft writes that devices on unsupported versions 'will lose access to Windows Update services'.
items.action: Report the installed update level per Windows build now and list every device below the update Microsoft names for it. After the expiry date the update has to come from the Microsoft Update Catalog or from your own management tools.

items.title: Graph what's new now lists merging incidents and moving alerts in v1.0, behind a permission that Microsoft's permissions reference does not carry
items.officialTitle: Security | Alerts and incidents
items.publishedNote: Microsoft files the entry under 'August 2026: New and generally available' and prints no day. 8 October 2026 is the day the entry appeared: it was absent at the 06:43 read and the documentation commit that adds it is 5a88c6f of 8 October 15:41 UTC.
items.fingerprint: Added to 'What's new in Microsoft Graph' under 'August 2026: New and generally available' between the 06:43 and the evening read of 8 October: 'Added the alert: moveAlerts and incident: mergeIncidents actions to support moving alerts and merging incidents in Microsoft Defender', the tenantId property on userAccount, the correlationReason enumeration and the mergeResponse resource. The two API pages give POST /security/alerts_v2/moveAlerts and POST /security/incidents/mergeIncidents, least privileged permission SecurityData.Manage.All for delegated and application access, and Security Operator as the least privileged role. The public documentation mirror shows both v1.0 pages in a commit of 17 June 2026; the what's-new line is what appeared today.
items.why: Merging folds separate incidents into one and a move takes an alert out of the incident an analyst is working, so whoever can call these two actions can rearrange the evidence of an investigation. The permission both pages name, SecurityData.Manage.All, is absent from Microsoft's permissions reference (972 names read today), from the service principal dump of 6 October and from the deployment map of 1 October, so this brief cannot say which permission ID grants it or whether it can be consented here.
items.action: Review who holds Security Operator and Security Administrator, the two roles Microsoft names for these actions, and watch the next service principal dump for SecurityData.Manage.All before searching consent grants for it.

items.tier0Note: It changes how an account password can be replaced: possession of one strong credential is enough, with no knowledge of the current password.
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft gives the end of October 2026 for the start of rollout, not a calendar date
items.title: My Sign-Ins will let a user with a passkey, FIDO2 key or Windows Hello set a new password without knowing the old one; rollout slips to the end of October and runs to the end of November, and the switch is tenant-wide only
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Allow password change after secure sign-in with My Sign-Ins
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised MC1437671 a second time on 9 October 2026 ('We have updated the content'): general availability, Worldwide and GCC, now begins at the 'end of October 2026 (previously mid-October)' and is 'expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)', and the feature is described throughout as 'password change after secure sign-in'. Unchanged from the 7 October revision: the feature is off by default, an administrator must turn it on, and 'The setting is tenant-wide: you can turn it on for your entire tenant or leave it off for everyone. There is no per-user or per-group scoping.' A user who has a passkey, FIDO2 security key or Windows Hello for Business can set a new password from My Sign-Ins without knowing the current one and without self-service password reset.
items.why: With the feature on, holding one phishing-resistant credential is enough to replace the account's password, so a passkey an attacker managed to register becomes a way to set a known password for anything that still accepts one. The control is all or nothing: privileged accounts cannot be left out.
items.action: Leave it off until the Learn page is published. If it is turned on, alert on a password change that follows a new passkey or FIDO2 registration on the same account within a short interval.

items.title: Sentinel gets an ASIM EmailEvent schema, and the ASIM parser list gains its first Agent Event parser
items.officialTitle: Introducing the Microsoft Sentinel ASIM EmailEvent schema
items.fingerprint: The Microsoft Sentinel blog of 7 October 2026 says the ASIM EmailEvent schema 'is now available', and the schema reference is on Learn: one normalised shape for email delivery and inspection records from mail servers, secure email gateways and email security services, with EventType and EventSubType, EmailFromAddress and EmailToRecipients, EmailSubject, EmailFiles and EmailUrls, SPF, DKIM and DMARC results, DvcAction and EmailDeliveryLocation. The ASIM parsers list, dated 7 October on Learn, gains an Agent Event parsers section with one source: Anthropic Claude Compliance events collected through the Codeless Connector Framework by BlueVoyant, parser _Im_AgentEvent_AnthropicClaudeCompliance. The parsers list names no EmailEvent source parser yet.
items.why: An email rule written against EmailEvents covers Defender for Office 365 only. A normalised schema lets one analytic rule read a third-party gateway and Defender together, with the email authentication results as named fields. No source parser is listed yet, so today the schema is a target to build to rather than something a rule can query.
items.action: No action required. If a secure email gateway feeds Sentinel, check whether its connector ships an EmailEvent parser before writing new email rules against the source tables.

items.officialTitleNote: Two Learn pages changed in two commits; Microsoft published no headline for the change, so the title above is this brief’s summary.
items.title: Microsoft removes the rollout notes from system-preferred authentication and the registration campaign: both are now documented as every tenant’s behaviour
items.fingerprint: Two Entra authentication pages lost their rollout notes on 7 October 2026 (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs 2f928bb and 8813cf4). The system-preferred authentication page no longer says the Microsoft managed state 'affects both first-factor and multifactor authentication and is being gradually deployed to tenants through September 2026'; the commit is titled 'Remove completed system-preferred rollout note'. The registration campaign page no longer says 'We're rolling out this version of the registration campaign. The rollout is expected to finish by the end of September 2026.' Neither page gained text.
items.why: Until yesterday a tenant that did not see system-preferred authentication at first factor, or the new registration campaign, could be told the rollout had not arrived. Microsoft's documentation now describes both as the behaviour of every tenant, so a difference is a configuration finding rather than something to wait for.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft. Where State is Microsoft managed, confirm on a test account that first-factor sign-in offers the strongest registered method, and compare the registration campaign that account sees with the page.

items.title: Defender for Office 365 starts detecting malicious URLs inside QR codes in Teams messages after delivery, and the detections reach Advanced Hunting
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Post-delivery protection for malicious QR codes in Microsoft Teams
items.fingerprint: Defender for Office 365 extends Teams URL protection to URLs inside QR codes. Teams messages containing a QR code are analysed after delivery; a malicious URL puts a warning on the message in external and in internal conversations, and with Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2 and Teams ZAP enabled eligible malicious internal messages may be blocked. Microsoft says the detections appear in Advanced Hunting 'with QRCode in the UrlLocation column of the MessageUrlInfo table'. General availability, Worldwide, from early October to early November 2026; it is part of existing Teams URL protection and has no separate setting. The MessageUrlInfo schema page on Learn, read on 8 October, lists six columns and UrlLocation is not yet among them.
items.why: A QR code was the way round URL scanning in Teams chat, because the link sits inside an image. This is the first time a QR-borne URL in Teams becomes a record a hunt can read, and the column Microsoft names for it is not in the published schema yet, so a query that names it directly may fail until the rollout reaches the tenant.
items.action: No action required by Microsoft. Confirm Teams ZAP is on, and add the QR code hunt in Hunting to the Teams phishing playbook; it is written to run before and after the UrlLocation column arrives.

items.title: Defender Vulnerability Management starts covering Node.js, Python and Java packages on Windows; assessment exports grow and gain a ProductCategory field
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management: Private preview for selected developer package vulnerability coverage
items.fingerprint: Defender Vulnerability Management adds CVE coverage for a curated set of Node.js, Python and Java packages on Windows devices onboarded to Defender for Endpoint: Targeted Release late September to late October, public preview late October to late November and general availability late November to late December 2026, Worldwide. Findings appear in the existing software component, vulnerability, affected device and recommendation views. A ProductCategory value separates Applications, Components and BIOS/firmware records; complete-file assessment exports for enabled tenants carry the full package population, JSON exports can be filtered server-side, and ProductCategory 'may not be enabled' in the Advanced Hunting tables during the initial preview. Microsoft states it is not an SBOM and carries no dependency graph, reachability analysis or package ownership.
items.why: Every pipeline that pulls vulnerability assessment exports into a SIEM, a data lake or a ticketing tool sees more rows per device once this is on, and the new rows are components rather than installed applications. A dashboard that counts vulnerable software per device changes its number with no new exposure behind it.
items.action: Record current export file sizes and ingestion times now. When the tenant is enabled, filter downloads by ProductCategory or apply Microsoft's Legacy Components Support List, and set a new baseline for any Delta integration.

items.title: Edge 157 retires the legacy direct-WAM sign-in on Windows in early November; every remaining profile moves to OneAuth and the opt-out switch stops working
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Edge: Retiring legacy sign-in implementation on Windows
items.fingerprint: From Microsoft Edge version 157 on Windows the legacy direct-WAM sign-in implementation is retired and all remaining profiles move to the OneAuth authentication library; the 'fallback legacy WAM path will default off under all circumstances', which includes organisations that disabled OneAuth with --disable-features=msOneAuthWAM. Windows Web Account Manager itself is not deprecated; OneAuth continues to use it. General availability, Worldwide and GCC, begins and completes in early November 2026. Microsoft says most users move transparently and in rare cases must sign in to Edge again. edge://signin-internals shows OneAuth or WAM under Edge Auth Library Information, and msedge.exe --enable-features=msForceOneAuthWAM tests the move on version 155 or later. Marked a major change.
items.why: Microsoft names browser sign-in, token fetch, single sign-on and account synchronisation as the affected experiences. A profile that loses its sign-in after the update stops presenting the signed-in work account to web applications, which reaches the SOC as extra prompts and Conditional Access failures rather than as an Edge fault (inferred).
items.action: Check edge://signin-internals on a sample of managed profiles, remove any --disable-features=msOneAuthWAM switch from deployment, and pilot msForceOneAuthWAM on Edge 155 or later before version 157 arrives in early November.

items.deadlineNote: Message Center's act-by date; Targeted release enrolment changes are disabled in November 2026 and Targeted release retires in January 2027
items.title: Targeted release retires in January 2027; enrolments freeze in November and Message Center asks for a decision by 31 October
items.officialTitle: Microsoft 365: Targeted Release retirement
items.fingerprint: Targeted release for Microsoft 365 retires in January 2027 and is replaced by three release options: Frontier (preview), Standard release (at general availability) and Deferred release (eligible major updates about 30 days after Standard release begins). In November 2026 administrators can no longer add, remove or modify Targeted release enrolments and a unified release preferences experience opens in the Microsoft 365 admin center; Message Center gives 31 October 2026 as the act-by date. Users already enrolled keep receiving Targeted release features until the retirement. Marked a major change; it names Teams, new Outlook, Outlook on the web, Office for the web, OneDrive, SharePoint Online and some components of Exchange Online.
items.why: Targeted release is how a pilot ring sees a change before the rest of the tenant, security-relevant changes included. From November the ring is frozen as it stands; from January the only early ring is Frontier, and Deferred release becomes the first option that holds a major update back by about 30 days.
items.action: Before 31 October export who is enrolled in Targeted release (Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences), decide which of them move to Frontier, and decide whether the tenant default becomes Standard or Deferred release.

items.tier0Note: A directory role now documented as managing application role assignments for Microsoft Graph and delegated permission grants is a route to tenant-wide privilege.
items.title: Tenant Governance Administrator is now documented with seven application-scoped operations, among them managing app role assignments for Microsoft Graph and delegated permission grants
items.officialTitle: Tenant Governance Administrator
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's role reference for Tenant Governance Administrator changed on 6 October 2026 (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs e673a48, ms.date 10/06/2026) and the change is live on Learn as read on 8 October. The Actions table is retitled 'Actions and operations' and gains seven rows marked application-scoped: create service principals, update service principal endpoints, delete, permanently delete and restore service principals, 'Manage delegated permission grants' and 'Manage application role assignments, including assignments for Microsoft Graph and Azure AD Graph'. Microsoft states that these operations 'are available only through the approved Tenant Governance application. Assigning this role does not grant equivalent unrestricted application-management permissions through other applications.' The 24 microsoft.directory and microsoft.office365 actions are unchanged and the role already carried the privileged label.
items.why: Granting an app role on Microsoft Graph and writing a delegated permission grant are the two operations that turn an application into a tenant-wide principal, and this role is now documented as reaching both through one Microsoft application. The seven rows are prose, not microsoft.directory action strings, so a tool that scans role definitions for dangerous actions does not see them.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft. List who holds Tenant Governance Administrator, put the assignment behind PIM with approval, and alert on the Entra audit activities 'Add app role assignment to service principal' and 'Add delegated permission grant' where the actor is a holder of this role or a Tenant Governance application.

items.title: Defender for Cloud: the new server security experience joins Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers data, and turning off Defender for Servers can offboard servers from Defender for Endpoint
items.officialTitle: New Defender server security experience
items.fingerprint: Defender for Cloud release notes, 6 October 2026, Public preview: 'The new Defender server security experience brings together cloud and endpoint data from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers.' In the Microsoft Defender portal: 'Review the new server asset page with combined cloud and endpoint details', investigate servers across alerts, incidents and the attack graph, use Go hunt, and 'Manage access with role-based access control (RBAC), server device groups, and cloud scopes.' In the Azure portal: 'Automatically offboard servers from Defender for Endpoint by turning off Defender for Servers plan for the subscription.' The entry was not on the page at the 06:42 read. On 7 October the Defender for Endpoint offboarding page gained an 'Automatic Azure offboarding' section: turning the plan off 'automatically offboards eligible servers from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint', changing from Plan 2 to Plan 1 or moving a machine between subscriptions does not trigger it, offboarding 'can take up to one hour for large subscriptions', and it 'doesn't uninstall the endpoint software or remove historical device records'. On 11 October 2026 Microsoft edited this entry on the published page: the first bullet read 'Review unified server inventory and combined cloud and endpoint details', the offboarding line read 'Automatically offboard eligible servers from Defender for Endpoint by turning off Defender for Servers for the subscription', and the entry gained the line 'Learn more about the new Defender server security experience', which links the Defender for Endpoint page azure-server-integration. Microsoft did not date the edit; the entry is still dated 6 October.
items.why: A plan switch on a subscription can now remove the endpoint sensor from its servers: turning off Defender for Servers offboards eligible servers from Defender for Endpoint. Who can see a server in the Defender portal is decided by device groups and cloud scopes together.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft. Find who holds the right to change Defender plans on each subscription, and alert on a Defender for Servers plan being turned off, since it now doubles as an EDR offboarding action.
items.fingerprintBefore: Defender for Cloud release notes, 6 October 2026, Public preview: 'The new Defender server security experience brings together cloud and endpoint data from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers.' In the Microsoft Defender portal: review unified server inventory, investigate servers across alerts, incidents and the attack graph, use Go hunt, and 'Manage access with role-based access control (RBAC), server device groups, and cloud scopes.' items.title: Conditional Access for agents: the prerequisite now names Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7, and a policy scoped through Users never reaches agent user accounts
items.officialTitle: Secure autonomous agents with Conditional Access
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no date for the change (inferred): entra-docs commits 965931b7ff and 6e8eb8aa25 of 7 October 2026, merged with pull request 14521 at 16:36 UTC, and read on the published Learn page the same evening.
items.fingerprint: Two Conditional Access pages for agent identities changed on 7 October 2026. Prerequisites of the autonomous-agents page read 'A Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license.' and 'Agent 365 license will soon be required'; they now read 'One of the following license plans: Microsoft 365 E7, which includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite, to protect access for both users and agents. Microsoft Agent 365, paired with: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 E3 for Conditional Access. Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft 365 E5 when using agent risk-based Conditional Access.' The companion page 'Conditional Access for agents' now states: 'Policies scoped through the "Users" assignment don't apply to agent user accounts. This boundary applies whether the policy targets all users, selected users, groups, directory roles, or external users.' and 'Selecting an agent identity as the policy subject doesn't cover agent requests made on behalf of the user.'
items.why: Two things a SOC assumes about Conditional Access stop being true for agents. A policy that targets agent identities is documented as needing Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7, where Entra ID P1 or P2 was listed alone; and an 'All users' policy does not cover an agent's user account however that account is selected. Microsoft does not state what happens to existing agent policies in a tenant without the licence.
items.action: List the Conditional Access policies that target agent identities or agent users, confirm the tenant holds Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7, and add a policy under Assignments, Agents, Agent Users wherever an all-users policy was assumed to cover agent user accounts.

items.title: Azure RBAC: Microsoft confirms customer-managed deny assignments exist in private preview, and warns that reference pages may already show the commands
items.officialTitle: List Azure deny assignments
items.publishedNote: The page's own date moved from 24 April 2025 to 6 October 2026 (azure-docs commit 3bd30651ed4c); it reached the main branch after the morning read and was read on the published Learn page on 7 October.
items.fingerprint: The Important note read 'You can't directly create your own deny assignments. Deny assignments are created and managed by Azure.' It now reads 'Customer-managed deny assignments are currently in private preview. The availability of related APIs or commands in generated reference documentation doesn't indicate that the feature is in public preview or generally available. For generally available scenarios, Azure creates and manages deny assignments.' The following section drops the sentence 'You can't directly create your own deny assignments.'
items.why: A deny assignment overrides every role assignment at its scope, Owner included. Microsoft now states that a tenant-authored form exists in private preview and that API or command reference may show it before release, so a deny assignment found in a subscription is no longer proof that Azure or a deployment stack wrote it. This moves an access control boundary, which is why it is weighted as identity and not as Azure platform.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft. Baseline the deny assignments that exist today per subscription (Get-AzDenyAssignment) so a later customer-written one stands out, and decide who would be allowed to write them before the feature reaches public preview.

items.title: Purview portal audit logs will record role and scoped-role access decisions (roadmap, government clouds, October 2026)
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Permissions audit log improvements
items.fingerprint: Roadmap entry 573447, created 6 October 2026, status In development, release phase General Availability, release date October CY2026, cloud instances GCC, GCC High and DoD, platform Web. Microsoft writes: 'Improving permission checks when users access the Microsoft Purview portal. Enhanced audit logs will provide clearer visibility into role and scoped-role access decisions, helping administrators troubleshoot access issues and monitor authorization outcomes.' The entry lists no Worldwide instance.

The entry is for the government clouds only; nothing in it says when or whether commercial tenants receive the same records.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Backup gains activity logs: who changed a backup policy or started a restore, filterable and exportable, from mid-October
items.officialTitle: Microsoft 365 Backup: Activity Logs
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 6 October 2026, category Stay informed, tags New feature, Feature update and User impact. 'We're introducing activity logs in Microsoft 365 Backup to help administrators monitor backup policy and restore activities directly within the product.' Entries cover SharePoint Online, OneDrive and Exchange Online and 'include metadata such as service, activity type, status, impact, policy or restore task details, timestamps, and the administrator who performed the action.' They can be filtered, searched and exported to CSV, and 'Role-based access controls will apply. Administrators will only be able to view logs for workloads they are authorized to manage.' General Availability (Worldwide) mid-October 2026; no action required. The page is Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 Backup, Recent activities.
items.why: A restore is a bulk write over production data and a backup policy change decides what can be recovered after ransomware, and until now neither had a log inside the product. The post does not say whether these events also reach the unified audit log, so the admin center page and its CSV export are the only place Microsoft has promised them.
items.action: After mid-October open Microsoft 365 Backup, Recent activities, confirm that policy changes and restores are listed with the administrator who made them, and decide whether the CSV export needs to be collected on a schedule until the same events are confirmed in the unified audit log.

items.title: Purview DLP for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business will work in tenants that use Intune multi-admin approval, and Purview can hand the Intune step to an Intune administrator as a task
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview DLP: Improved setup and Intune multi-admin approval support for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 6 October 2026, tag Admin impact. Microsoft Purview will 'support tenants that use Intune multi-admin approval' when data loss prevention for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business is set up, and the portal will show 'clearer setup status information, more detailed error information, and guidance'. A Purview administrator can 'send a task to the appropriate Intune administrator'; Microsoft adds that this 'does not grant permissions, bypass approval requirements, or automatically complete requested Intune changes.' Worldwide rollout early November to mid-November 2026; 'No action is required before rollout.'

Microsoft says the hand-off does not bypass approval, which is the sentence to hold it to: after rollout, an approval request raised from Purview is a new way for an Intune change to be asked for.
items.action: If Intune multi-admin approval is on, tell the approvers that requests originating from the Purview portal will begin to appear in November, and check after rollout that the setup status in Purview matches what Intune actually applied.

This is a targeted migration extension, not a change to the previously announced retirement for other customers.' Which one is true depends on the Entra ID Governance licence, and a tenant that plans on the extension without holding the licence gets frozen group membership with no error.

items.title: Microsoft corrected PIM for Groups: eligible members and owners are credential-protected too, and changing those credentials needs Privileged Authentication Administrator
items.officialTitle: What is Privileged Identity Management for groups?
items.tier0Note: The article governs who may reset the credentials of members and owners of a role-assignable group, which is the write path used to elevate into Entra roles including Global Administrator.
items.fingerprint: Pull request 2049 reached entra-docs main at 16:57 UTC on 23 September 2026 and the live branch at 17:42 UTC. It widened the stated protection of role-assignable groups from active members to members and owners including eligible ones who have not activated, and it replaced the Helpdesk Administrator example in the security note with a general statement plus a new sentence naming Privileged Authentication Administrator as the least role that can change those credentials. The include file's ms.date moved from 01/31/2023 to 07/29/2026.
items.why: The previous wording left open the classic PIM-for-Groups attack: a lower-privileged admin resets the password of a user who is only an eligible member of a role-assignable group, then activates the assignment on their behalf. Microsoft now states that the credential protection already covers eligible members and owners, so that path is closed by the platform — but only for groups that were actually created as role-assignable.
items.action: Confirm that every group used to elevate into an Entra role is role-assignable (isAssignableToRole true). A group that is not gets none of this protection, and the eligible-member reset path is still open on it. No deadline is stated by Microsoft.

items.title: Microsoft corrects what PIM for Groups actually protects: eligible members and owners were always in scope, and non-role-assignable groups never were
items.officialTitle: Privileged Identity Management for Groups
items.publishedNote: The page still prints ms.date 23 April 2026; the correction reached the public entra-docs live branch on 22 September 2026 and Microsoft did not bump the printed date.
items.tier0Note: The corrected sentence describes who can reset the credentials of a user who can elevate to an Entra role.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft replaced the statement that for role-assignable groups no other users can change the credentials of the users who are active members, with: credential protection covers the members and owners of the group, including eligible members and owners who have not activated yet. The accompanying note adds that groups used for role elevation must be created as role-assignable, and that changing the credentials of members and owners of a role-assignable group requires at least the Privileged Authentication Administrator role.
items.why: The old sentence understated the protection in one direction and overstated it in another. The practical consequence is the second half: a group that grants an Entra role but was not created role-assignable gives its eligible members no credential protection at all, so a Helpdesk, Authentication or User Administrator can reset their password and then elevate. That is a documented escalation path, and it is a configuration mistake rather than a vulnerability.
items.action: List every group that grants an Entra role and check isAssignableToRole on each. Any that is false is the finding; it cannot be changed after creation, so the group has to be recreated as role-assignable and the assignments moved.

items.title: Eight Graph permissions became grantable in the service principal: app certificate trust configuration, cross-tenant content migration and workbooks
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no announcement for this; the change is visible only as a diff of the Microsoft Graph service principal.
items.reference: no MC/RM post — service principal only
items.tier0Note: AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All writes the tenant's application certificate trust configuration, which governs which certificates an application may authenticate with.
items.fingerprint: Between the 17 September and the 22 September dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal, application roles went from 741 to 747 and delegated scopes from 825 to 827, with nothing removed. The six new application roles are AppCertTrustConfiguration.Read.All, AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All, CrossTenantContentMigration.Read.All, CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All, Workbooks.Read.All and Workbooks.ReadWrite.All; the two new delegated scopes are Workbooks.Read.All and Workbooks.ReadWrite.All. All eight are enabled. AppCertTrustConfiguration had existed as a delegated scope since 9 May 2026 but reaches application scope only now.
items.why: Two of the eight are a consent surface worth naming. AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All is application-scoped write access to the tenant's app certificate trust configuration — the setting that decides which certificates an application may present to authenticate — so an app holding it can widen what counts as a trusted credential. CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All is an application-scoped write over content moving between tenants, which is a bulk data path rather than a single-object one.
items.action: Nothing is granted by this change. Add all six application roles to the consent-review list now, before the first grant request arrives, and decide in advance which of them may ever be consented and by whom. Workbooks.* is the least alarming of the three families; the two AppCertTrustConfiguration roles are the ones to treat as privileged.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no title for this: the names are read out of the Graph service principal, which Microsoft does not document until later. The heading shown is the dump commit this brief read.
items.tier0Note: Ten scopes an application can be consented to today, one of which reads every group membership in the tenant and two of which rewrite the rules governing access to protected content.
items.why: Two of them stand out. GroupMember.ReadBasic.All reads every group membership in the organisation as an application, with no signed-in user — that is the whole org chart and the membership of every privileged access group, in one call. And InfoProtectABACPolicy.ReadWrite.All plus InfoProtectAttributeAssignment.ReadWrite.All together let a holder define an attribute, assign it to a principal and thereby grant access to protected content without touching a group, a role or a label.
items.action: Put all ten appRoleIds on the consent-alert list today, ahead of the documentation. The two that matter most are 8222c640-cae5-4860-8d11-b32cfad95e03 (GroupMember.ReadBasic.All) and 4bfc1735-3a0c-4602-a159-9cfa07213339 (InfoProtectABACPolicy.ReadWrite.All). Then ask Purview whether an ABAC policy catalog is being enabled in this tenant, because nothing else has announced it.

items.title: September update makes Windows 11 honour Machine Identity Isolation; devices not on a Windows Server 2025 domain functional level lose domain trust
items.officialTitle: Domain-joined devices might lose their secure trust relationship with the domain
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Windows release health
items.fingerprint: Opened 16 September 2026 (status Mitigated): after KB5124008 (24H2/25H2) or KB5124012 (26H1) and later updates, Windows begins honouring existing or policy-provisioned Machine Identity Isolation enforcement. The feature is supported only with domain controllers at Windows Server 2025 domain functional level; elsewhere Credential Guard protected machine accounts can lose their secure channel and users cannot sign in with valid domain credentials. Cached sign-in may still work; AD replication is not affected. Workaround: set MachineIdentityIsolation to 0 by the method that enabled it, restart, then run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair. Microsoft plans to temporarily block enforcement in a future update.
items.why: A help-desk wave of 'trust relationship failed' sign-in errors after Patch Tuesday is this known issue, not an attack — but only if Machine Identity Isolation was enabled somewhere.
items.action: Find every Intune or Group Policy setting that enables Machine Identity Isolation; unless all DCs run Windows Server 2025 DFL, set it to 0 and repair the secure channel.

items.title: Six Secure Score recommendations are grouped as an AI-Readiness device baseline, four of them new
items.officialTitle: New Microsoft Secure Score recommendations for AI-Readiness
items.fingerprint: Microsoft groups six device recommendations under an AI-Readiness tag in Exposure Management > Recommendations > Devices > Misconfigurations. Four are new: establish a hardware root of trust with TPM 2.0; isolate critical security functions with VBS; enforce kernel code integrity with HVCI; limit lateral movement with Windows LAPS. Two already existed: reduce unnecessary internet exposure on internet-facing devices, and protect the startup process with Secure Boot. The view shows affected devices, exposed critical devices, points achieved and the impact on the Devices Secure Score.
items.why: This is a named, filterable hardening baseline rather than six unrelated recommendations, and Windows LAPS plus HVCI are the two that most directly cut the paths an intruder uses after a first foothold. The AI-Readiness framing is Microsoft's; the controls underneath it are ordinary endpoint hardening.
items.action: Filter Recommendations > Devices > Misconfigurations by the AI-Readiness tag and read the exposed-critical-devices count first, not the score. Where Windows LAPS is not deployed on that set, that is the one to schedule.
