items.title: Global Secure Access allows up to ten custom Private Access forwarding profiles, and priority decides which one applies
items.officialTitle: Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles
items.tier0Note: A forwarding profile decides which users reach which private applications, so its priority is an access control.
items.fingerprint: Tenants can create custom Private Access traffic forwarding profiles in addition to the single default one, up to ten during preview. Each custom profile carries its own acquisition rules, assignments, status and priority, and profiles can be assigned to users, groups, devices and device platforms, with nested group membership supported. When several enabled profiles for the same traffic type apply to a user and device, only the applicable profile with the highest priority is used. Deleted custom profiles cannot be restored.
items.why: Priority is now the thing that decides who reaches which private application, and priority is a field rather than an assignment. A change to it re-scopes access without any assignment changing, which is invisible to a review that reads assignments only.
items.action: Add create, modify and delete of traffic forwarding profiles to Global Secure Access audit log monitoring, and treat a priority change as an access change in review. The stated use case — excluding privileged applications from a broadly assigned profile — is worth building deliberately rather than inheriting.

items.title: Azure Blueprints stops accepting new assignments on 31 October, and its resource locks stop working at full retirement
items.officialTitle: Azure Blueprints retirement
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date on the retirement page; the timeline has been extended more than once since the original 2023 announcement.
items.deadlineNote: 31 Oct 2026 ends modification of blueprint definitions and creation of new assignments; 31 Dec 2026 ends modification of existing assignments; 31 Jan 2027 is full retirement, when the API stops responding and unexported content is permanently deleted.
items.fingerprint: Phased retirement. From 31 October 2026 existing blueprint definitions can no longer be modified and new blueprint assignments can no longer be created. From 31 December 2026 existing assignments can no longer be modified. On 31 January 2027 the API stops responding, the CLI and PowerShell commands stop, Blueprints is removed from the portal, and unexported definitions, versions and assignments are permanently deleted.
items.why: Blueprint assignments can apply Do Not Delete and Read Only locks. Those locks stop functioning at retirement, so any resource whose protection rests on a blueprint lock silently loses it — and the definitions that describe what was being protected are deleted at the same time.
items.action: Export every blueprint definition, version and assignment you intend to keep before 31 January 2027, and before 31 October decide the replacement for each lock: Azure Policy deny or denyAction for the rule, and a resource lock for the deletion protection.

items.title: Conditional Access docs turn the unverified device-platform note into a warning and tell admins to pair the condition with compliance to stop user-agent spoofing
items.officialTitle: Conditional Access: Conditions
items.fingerprint: On 28 September 2026 Microsoft turned the existing Device platforms paragraph of Conditional Access: Conditions (platform read from user agent strings, which can be modified, so the information is not verified) into a WARNING box and added one sentence: use Conditional Access policies with this condition together with another policy, such as one requiring device compliance or app protection, to mitigate the risk of user agent spoofing.
items.fingerprintBefore: Plain paragraph: the device platform comes from information the device provides, such as user agent strings, which can be modified, so it is not verified; use it with Intune compliance or as part of a block statement.
items.why: The caveat is a year old, but Microsoft has now made it a warning and named the attack: user agent spoofing. A policy that grants or exempts on device platform alone can be satisfied by an attacker who changes a user agent string.
items.action: List Conditional Access policies whose only distinguishing condition is Device platforms and whose grant is not Block; pair each with device compliance or app protection, or turn it into a block statement.
items.sourceCommit: MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs b86e263a1b, 28 September 2026: Enhance device platform section with security note (#2112)
items.tier0Note: Conditional Access is the gate in front of every privileged sign-in; a condition that can be spoofed is a bypass if it is the only condition.

items.title: Exchange Online PowerShell enforces stricter sign-in from 31 March 2027; ExchangeOnlineManagement below 3.10.1 can fail to authenticate

items.fingerprint: Security enhancements to Exchange Online PowerShell authentication shipped in ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.1; from 31 March 2027 earlier versions may fail interactive authentication, particularly PowerShell 7 with Web Account Manager disabled. items.title: Passkeys for B2B guests: a resource tenant will issue its own passkeys to guest users, on by default
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra ID: Passkey support for B2B users
items.fingerprint: Roadmap 569432, created 1 October 2026, status In development, release phase General Availability: B2B users, internal guests and external users alike, will register and sign in with passkeys issued by the resource tenant to meet that tenant's MFA requirement, from My Security Info, an in-line proof-up prompt or a passkey registration campaign. The change is on by default; B2B users already in scope for passkeys in the Authentication methods policy are enabled automatically.
items.why: A guest will hold a phishing-resistant credential that lives in your tenant rather than in theirs. That closes the gap in which guests satisfied MFA only through their home tenant, and it also means guest accounts start carrying authentication methods your tenant must govern, audit and revoke.
items.action: Review who the passkey (FIDO2) policy in Authentication methods targets today: if it targets All users, guests are in scope the day this ships. Decide whether guests should register resource-tenant passkeys, then adjust the target groups, the registration campaign and the Conditional Access policies before rollout.

items.title: Exchange Server gets a V2 of the September security updates: CVE-2026-96940 lets a signed-in user read other people's mailboxes
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Exchange Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
items.fingerprint: MSRC published CVE-2026-96940 on 2 October 2026, outside the monthly cadence: weak authorization in Exchange Server lets an authenticated attacker gain access to other users' mailboxes in the same organization and read messages and attachments. Important, CVSS 8.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N), Exploited: No, Publicly disclosed: No, Exploitation More Likely. Fixed builds: Exchange SE RTM 15.02.2562.053 (KB5129955), 2019 CU15 15.02.1748.053 (KB5129956), 2019 CU14 15.02.1544.048 (KB5129957), 2016 CU23 15.01.2507.075 (KB5129958); the 2016 and 2019 updates are available only under the Period 2 ESU program. Exchange Online already carries a service-side fix. The Exchange Team blog says the only difference between the 24 September release and V2 is this CVE.
items.why: A server patched with the 24 September set is not patched for this. Any valid low-privilege mailbox account is enough to read another mailbox, Microsoft rates exploitation as more likely, and a server that reports the September update as installed will look compliant unless the build number is checked.
items.action: Run the Exchange Health Checker and confirm every Exchange SE, 2019 and 2016 server is on the 2 October build (SE RTM 15.02.2562.053 or the matching 2019/2016 ESU build), not the 24 September one; treat a server still on the earlier build as unpatched.

items.title: Security Operator loses default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List under Defender Unified RBAC, from early November
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Changes to Unified RBAC permission mapping for Microsoft Entra Security Operator role
items.fingerprint: From early November 2026 the default Unified RBAC mapping of the Entra Security Operator role for Defender for Office 365 no longer includes Authorization and settings\Security settings (All permissions). Where Unified RBAC is enabled for Email & Collaboration, Security Operator alone will no longer view, create, edit or delete anti-spam, anti-phishing, anti-malware, Safe Links, Safe Attachments or preset security policies, nor view or change Tenant Allow/Block List entries. items.title: Private Access Sensor 2.2.79 for domain controllers: updates now install themselves, the local registry break-glass override is gone, and Kerberos enforcement extends to UDP
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra Private Access Sensor release history — Version 2.2.79
items.tier0Note: The sensor is installed on domain controllers and enforces Kerberos policy there; from 2.2.79 future sensor builds download and install themselves on that host. Tier-0 classification of the host is this brief's (inferred).
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's release history page gained a Version 2.2.79 section on 5 October 2026 (entra-docs commit 3977e05ee); Microsoft dates the release itself 29 September 2026. The release adds automatic download and installation of future sensor updates; upgrading from 2.2.42 needs a one-time install of the full installer from the Entra admin center to enable over-the-air updates. Security enhancements: Kerberos policy enforcement extends to UDP alongside TCP, network packet validation is hardened and the local registry break-glass override is removed in favor of cloud policy. Non-wildcard SPNs and requested Kerberos service names are now matched by the owning Active Directory account SID, which extends protection to aliases of the same account. Upgrade considerations: allow inbound TCP and UDP on port 1337; IPv6 Kerberos traffic is unsupported and blocked.
items.why: The Private Access Sensor runs on domain controllers and decides which Kerberos requests are allowed, so three things change on a tier-0 host at once: the sensor now updates itself from the cloud, the on-box registry override an administrator could use to bypass enforcement in an outage no longer exists, and Kerberos over UDP is enforced where only TCP was. A site that relied on the registry break-glass has lost its local way out, and an IPv6-only Kerberos path stops working.
items.action: List the domain controllers that run the Private Access Sensor and their versions; before upgrading from 2.2.42 open inbound TCP and UDP 1337, confirm no client depends on Kerberos over IPv6, replace any runbook step that uses the registry break-glass with the cloud policy equivalent, and decide who approves self-installing updates on domain controllers.
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints 'Released for download on September 29, 2026'; the section reached the page with entra-docs commit 3977e05ee on 5 October 2026 and was read on the published Learn page on 6 October.

items.title: Outlook on the web and new Outlook will block .msix and .msixbundle attachments by default from early November, in every OWA mailbox policy
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Outlook: Update to default blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 5 October 2026, flagged a major change: the .msix and .msixbundle file types are added to the BlockedFileTypes list in the default OWA mailbox policy and in any custom policies in the tenant. Rollout for Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026. Users of Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will no longer be able to open or download those attachments. Organizations that rely on them should add them to the AllowedFileTypes property of the users' OwaMailboxPolicy before rollout.

The cost falls on teams that distribute line-of-business app packages by mail, which will fail without an error anyone anticipated, and the change reaches custom policies too, not only the default one.
items.action: Search mail flow for .msix and .msixbundle attachments over the last 90 days; if a business process depends on them, move it off email rather than adding the types to AllowedFileTypes, and record the decision before early November.

It doesn't deploy or license the full Defender for Endpoint experience. The server still requires connectivity to Defender for Endpoint cloud services because the underlying Sense component uses that infrastructure.' The callout changed from Important to Note. items.title: Final reminder: the MemberOf rule operator stops processing on 3 November, and dynamic groups built on it freeze in their last state
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra ID: Final reminder to replace MemberOf rule operator configurations by November 3, 2026
items.fingerprint: Message Center post of 5 October 2026, category Retirement, action required by 3 November 2026: Microsoft is retiring the MemberOf rule operator in Microsoft Entra ID. Organizations using it in dynamic groups, administrative units or entitlement policies must replace those configurations before the deadline. After retirement, 'Dynamic groups using MemberOf will stop processing membership changes' and 'existing membership and assignment data will remain in their last known state.' Microsoft's required actions: identify every MemberOf configuration, replace it with supported operators where feasible, convert to assigned membership where no alternative exists, validate, and remove obsolete configurations.
items.why: A group that stops recalculating does not fail loudly: it keeps whoever was in it on 3 November. A leaver stays in a group that grants access or a licence, a joiner never arrives in a group a Conditional Access policy targets, and an administrative unit stops following the population it was meant to scope. Nothing alerts, because nothing errors.
items.action: Query dynamic groups and administrative units for membership rules containing memberOf, list which Conditional Access policies, access packages and licence assignments target them, and replace each rule or convert the group to assigned membership before 3 November.

items.title: Twelve Graph permissions became grantable: write access to provisioning-job synchronization metadata, Sentinel Content Hub packages and tenant-defined custom objects
items.tier0Note: SynchronizationMetadata.ReadWrite.All and .ReadWrite.OwnedBy delete object connections of service principal provisioning jobs; Entra-to-Active-Directory provisioning runs as such a job, so the linkage to on-premises accounts is in reach (inferred — Microsoft's description does not name which jobs are in scope).
items.fingerprint: Between the 29 September and the 5 October dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal (merill/microsoft-info 4f54a87 to 974a2dd, 23:16 UTC), application roles went from 748 to 760 and delegated scopes from 828 to 838, with nothing removed. The twelve new application roles are SynchronizationMetadata.Read.All, .Read.OwnedBy, .ReadWrite.All and .ReadWrite.OwnedBy; ContentHub-Catalog.Read.All, ContentHub-Installed.Read.All and ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All; CustomObject.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All; CustomObjectDefinition.Read.All, .ReadBasic.All and .ReadWrite.All. Ten of them also arrive as delegated scopes requiring admin consent; the two OwnedBy roles are application only. All are enabled, none is in the permissions reference, and all twelve had been in Microsoft's deployment map since September or earlier. Afternoon pass, 6 October: the next dump of the same service principal (merill/microsoft-info 531674a, 12:09 UTC) does not carry the twelve names and is byte-identical to the dumps of 29 September and 1 October, 748 application roles and 828 delegated scopes. One read holds them and the next does not, so treat them as rolling out and not as settled; the catalog entries are left as the morning wrote them until a third read decides. Read again on 7 October: the dump of 6 October 12:09 UTC (531674a) had gone back to 748 application roles and 828 delegated scopes without the twelve, and the next one, 6 October 21:48 UTC (9c21ffa), carries 760 and 838 again with all twelve names. Two of three consecutive dumps hold them, which is what a ring-by-ring deployment looks like from one replica.

SynchronizationMetadata.ReadWrite.All lets an app 'read, delete object connections, and manage synchronization job metadata and linkage information across all service principal provisioning jobs' without a signed-in user; deleting the link between a source identity and the account provisioned from it is how a provisioning job is made to lose track of an account. ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All can 'create, update, and delete installed packages and package-scoped content items', which is the installed security content of the organization. CustomObjectDefinition.ReadWrite.All manages a directory data surface Microsoft has not documented.
items.action: Nothing is granted by this change. Add the twelve application role IDs and ten delegated scope IDs from the Graph API tab to the consent watch list today, and run the hunting query in Hunting & actions to confirm none has been assigned since 29 September.

items.title: Microsoft's Graph permissions reference documents 33 more permissions, among them the thirteen that delete users' authentication methods, four identity-diagnostic names and four Customer Lockbox names
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Graph permissions reference
items.tier0Note: Thirteen of the 33 are application roles that delete authentication methods of every user, Global Administrators included; removing the strong method on a privileged account is a step toward taking it over.
items.fingerprint: Commit 5a88c6f of 8 October 2026 15:41 UTC took Microsoft's permissions-reference.md from 939 to 972 permission sections (524,219 to 540,216 bytes); with the 58 resource-specific-consent rows the reference now documents 1,030 names. Added: UserAuthenticationMethod.Delete.All and twelve UserAuthMethod-*.Delete.All names (Email, External, HardwareOATH, MicrosoftAuthApp, Passkey, Phone, PlatformCred, QR, ResourceKey, SoftwareOATH, TAP, WindowsHello), all application-only with admin consent; IdentityDiagnostic.Read, .Read.All, .StartDiagnosis and .StartDiagnosis.All; LockboxRequest and LockboxSettings Read.All and ReadWrite.All; AgentCommunicationConfiguration x4; LifecyclePolicies-AgentId x2; DeviceManagementDeploymentPlans x2; PullPrintPrinter x3; PreAuthorizationGrant.Read.All. Microsoft's text for the passkey one: 'Allows the application to delete passkey authentication methods of all users in your organization, without a signed-in user.' No permission was removed.
items.why: Every one of these names was already in this catalog, read from the service principal or from Microsoft's deployment map weeks before the page carried it, so nothing new became grantable today. What changed is that an approver can now look the name up, and that a consent review built from the documentation gains 33 rows it did not have. The delete-only family grants no read and no write, so a review that searches for ReadWrite on authentication methods still does not find it.
items.action: Add the 33 names and their identifiers to the consent-review list from the Graph API tab, then query app role assignments for the thirteen authentication-method delete roles and confirm that only a joiner-mover-leaver tool holds any of them.

items.title: Policy.ReadWrite.Recovery is now documented as an application permission too: the organization's recovery policy becomes writable without a signed-in user

Until then the section listed the delegated scope only (1e7a2f4c-e602-4b1b-9547-304dd65c4cc2). The application role is not in the Graph service principal dump of 6 October, the newest one published.

The reference is ahead of the service principal here, so the first tenant grant will come after a ring deployment, with no announcement (inferred from the two sources disagreeing).
items.action: Put identifier 795fc94d-3deb-4632-b1eb-e6d1a5f44918 on the app-role-assignment watchlist now, before the role is grantable in your tenant.

items.title: Microsoft now writes it down: an application with User.ReadWrite.All can update users who hold privileged admin roles
items.officialTitle: Overview of Microsoft Graph permissions
items.tier0Note: Microsoft states that the application permission reaches users assigned privileged admin roles, which makes an application holding it a path to those accounts.
items.fingerprint: Added to 'Overview of Microsoft Graph permissions' in commit 5a88c6f of 8 October 2026: 'With the User.ReadWrite.All application permission, an application can update many of the writable user properties supported by Microsoft Graph, including for users assigned privileged admin roles.' and 'Application permissions are highly privileged because they allow applications to access and modify resources without requiring a signed-in user. From a least-privilege perspective, the delegated permission model is the recommended approach whenever it meets the application's requirements.' Nothing in the permission itself changed; the sentence is new.
items.why: This is the vendor's own statement of something tenants routinely under-rate: User.ReadWrite.All as an application role is not a help-desk permission. It is the sentence to quote when an integration asks for it.
items.action: List every service principal holding the User.ReadWrite.All application role and treat each as a tier-0 identity: owner, credential type, and Conditional Access for workload identities where licensed.

items.title: MailboxItem.ImportExport and MailboxItem.ImportExport.All are relabelled from 'backup and restore' to 'export and import' of mailbox items
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Graph permissions reference — MailboxItem.ImportExport
items.fingerprint: Same identifiers, new consent text, in commit 5a88c6f of 8 October 2026. MailboxItem.ImportExport.All: 'Export and import all the users' mailbox items' and 'Allows the app to export and import all the users' mailbox items, without signed-in user.', where it read 'Allows the app to perform backup and restore for all mailbox items'. The delegated MailboxItem.ImportExport changed the same way.
items.why: The new label says what the role always allowed. An application role that exports every mailbox is the most direct mail-exfiltration grant Graph has, and any review note or detection that matches on the old display text no longer matches.
items.action: Confirm that every holder of MailboxItem.ImportExport.All is a known backup or migration product, and update consent-review text that quoted the old wording.

items.title: Entra Kerberos gets one configuration guide: the key-rotation page is folded into it, with a stated rotation practice and a warning that only Set-AzureADKerberosServer may rotate the key
items.officialTitle: Configure Microsoft Entra Kerberos trust
items.tier0Note: The Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object lives in on-premises Active Directory and its key protects the ticket-granting tickets Entra ID issues; the page describes it as functioning like a read-only domain controller.
items.fingerprint: Revised 21 October 2026 (commit 42c3495, ms.date 10/19/2026): the page no longer says on-premises AD DS trusts Microsoft Entra ID. It now states the procedure creates a Trusted Domain Object in AD DS for the realm KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM, inbound from the AD DS domain's perspective, so Microsoft Entra ID trusts AD-issued cross-realm referral tickets, which AD-authenticated clients use to get service tickets from Entra ID for Azure Files and Azure SQL Managed Instance. New note: the Trusted Domain Object is not required for Windows Hello for Business cloud Kerberos trust or FIDO2 sign-in to on-premises resources, which need only the Kerberos server object (Set-AzureADKerberosServer without -SetupCloudTrust).
items.why: A trust whose direction was described backwards gets reviewed backwards: the Trusted Domain Object is an object in AD DS that lets Entra ID accept AD-issued referrals, and tenants that only need Windows Hello cloud Kerberos trust or FIDO2 do not need it at all.
items.action: Check whether a KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM Trusted Domain Object exists in each forest (Get-ADTrust), keep it only where Azure Files or SQL MI need it, and treat it as a tier-0 object in AD monitoring.
items.fingerprintBefore: Commit 1c41e71 of 8 October 2026 adds 'Configure Microsoft Entra Kerberos trust' (305 lines, ms.date 10/07/2026), removes 'Rotate the Kerberos server key' and redirects it to the new page. The new page covers creating the Trusted Domain Object, client configuration, key rotation, and removing the object. On rotation: 'Microsoft doesn't mandate a fixed rotation interval. Rotate the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server key on the same schedule as other Active Directory Kerberos (krbtgt) keys, during scheduled security maintenance windows, and immediately after a suspected credential compromise.' And: 'Other tools can rotate krbtgt keys, but you must use the Set-AzureADKerberosServer cmdlet for the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server.'

items.title: Conditional Access baseline-scope enforcement: the page now speaks of the rollout in the past tense and adds a Graph query that lists the policies it affects
items.officialTitle: Conditional Access enforcement for resource exclusions (baseline scopes)
items.fingerprint: Commit 3c73d53 of 8 October 2026, 'Revise enforcement model details and rollout date': 'Rollout of the enforcement model for baseline scopes began on June 15, 2026' where the page read 'begins'; 'If you haven't made any changes to the baseline scopes settings, the enforcement is enabled automatically', with the words 'over a period of approximately several weeks' removed. Added: a Graph query, conditionalAccess/policies filtered on includeApplications 'All' with any excludeApplications, that lists the All-resources policies with at least one resource exclusion; and the sign-in log example now spans 15 June to 15 July 2026. No new date is stated.
items.why: Sign-ins that request only baseline scopes used to pass an All-resources policy that carried exclusions; with enforcement they must satisfy it. The page no longer describes that as upcoming, so an unexplained Conditional Access prompt or failure on such an application is now expected behaviour rather than a fault.
items.action: Run the Graph query Microsoft added to list the policies in scope, and filter sign-in logs on the placeholder audience to see which applications are affected in your tenant.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft's own date: 'Beginning January 1, 2027'; rollout early to mid-January 2027.
items.title: Viva Glint survey mail will come from the tenant's default domain from 1 January 2027 unless a custom sending domain is configured
items.officialTitle: Viva Glint: Change to the default email sending domain
items.fingerprint: Message Center, 8 October 2026: 'Beginning January 1, 2027, Viva Glint survey notification emails will use your organization's default domain if you have not configured a custom sending domain in the M365 admin center, instead of no-reply@glint.mail.microsoft. Your default domain may look like contoso.onmicrosoft.com.' Microsoft adds that 'Email filtering rules that reference the current sender may need to be updated' and asks that allow-list changes be scoped 'to your specific sending domain—not all of onmicrosoft.com'.
items.why: Survey mail with links, arriving from an onmicrosoft.com address, is what users are trained to report and what transport rules are written to quarantine. The safe fix is a verified custom domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, not a broad allow-list entry.
items.action: If Viva Glint is in use, configure the custom sending domain and validate SPF, DKIM and DMARC before January; refuse any request to allow-list onmicrosoft.com as a whole.

items.title: Windows 11 26H2 security baseline is reissued as v2: Administrator protection is now part of it, with credential prompts on the secure desktop
items.officialTitle: Windows 11, version 26H2 security baseline
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Baselines Blog, as it stood in the feed on 8 October 2026: 'The Windows 11, version 26H2 security baseline has been updated to reflect the general availability of Administrator protection. An updated v2 package is now available, and organizations should review and test the existing Administrator protection configuration as appropriate for their environment.' Marked updated in the change table: 'User Account Control: Configure type of Admin Approval Mode' is 'Admin Approval Mode with Administrator protection', and the elevation prompt for administrators is 'Prompt for credentials on the secure desktop'. Also in the baseline: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 in place of TLS 1.1 and 1.2 for the Internet Control Panel setting, and Windows Ready Print driver ranking enabled.
items.why: Administrator protection replaces the split-token admin session with a separate, just-in-time elevation that asks for credentials. A baseline that enables it changes how every local-admin elevation looks in the logs and breaks tools that relied on silent elevation.
items.action: Take the v2 package from the Security Compliance Toolkit, test Administrator protection on admin workstations first, and brief the help desk on the new credential prompt.

items.title: A Purview DLP policy can now keep Microsoft 365 Copilot from grounding answers in mail received from external senders
items.officialTitle: Protecting Organizations from External Email Risks in Microsoft 365 Copilot
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Community blog, 8 October 2026: 'A new policy in Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) addresses exactly this challenge. It lets organizations ground Copilot in trusted internal email only—reducing the risk of cross-prompt injection'. It is configured as 'a DLP policy configured in the Microsoft Purview portal using the "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat" policy location with the "Email is received from > External users" condition', and 'With this new policy enabled, the external email is excluded from grounding entirely'. The post states no licence requirement and no rollout date in the part this brief read.
items.why: Indirect prompt injection through an inbound message is the attack on Copilot that needs no access to the tenant at all. This is a tenant-side control for it that does not depend on detecting the injected text.
items.action: Pilot the policy on a group that receives a lot of external mail and measure what Copilot stops being able to answer before widening it.

items.title: Purview DLP can stop Copilot from using external web search for a prompt that contains sensitive information types
items.officialTitle: Why DLP for External Web Search in Microsoft 365 Copilot Matters?
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Community blog, 8 October 2026: the feature 'keeps sensitive information from reaching external web search during Copilot's query generation'. In Microsoft's summary, 'admin and user toggles decide whether Copilot can search the web; Microsoft Purview DLP decides what data may leave when it does', and it 'Prevents Copilot from using external web search as a grounding source for that prompt. It does not block the prompt itself'. The post also restates that generated queries, not whole prompts or files, go to the Bing search service with user and tenant identifiers removed.
items.why: Until now the web-search control for Copilot was on or off. A content-aware control means web grounding can stay enabled for ordinary work while a prompt carrying a card number or a passport number stays inside the tenant boundary.
items.action: Add the Copilot location to the DLP policy that already defines your sensitive information types, in audit mode first, and review matches for a week.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no announcement for this; the change is visible only as a diff of the Microsoft Graph service principal.
items.tier0Note: AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All creates, updates and deletes the trusted issuers that restrict which identity providers can be used in federated identity credentials, without a signed-in user; that list is a control on the workload-identity federation path (inferred from Microsoft's description in the service principal; Microsoft has published no documentation for the feature).
items.publishedNote: The day of the first service principal dump that holds the names (merill/microsoft-info cf0307f, 9 October 2026 21:49 UTC); Microsoft prints no date for them.
items.reference: no MC/RM post — service principal only
items.title: Seven Graph permissions became grantable and two gained a delegated scope: the trusted-issuer list for federated identity credentials, Copilot spending policies and cross-tenant content migration
items.fingerprint: Between the 6 October and the 9 October dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal (merill/microsoft-info 9c21ffa to cf0307f, 21:49 UTC), application roles went from 760 to 762 and delegated scopes from 838 to 847, with nothing removed; distinct names went from 999 to 1,006. New as an application role and a delegated scope: AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.Read.All and AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All. New as delegated scopes only: CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All, CopilotCostManagement-Policy.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All, and CopilotCostManagement-UserData.Read.All. CrossTenantContentMigration.Read.All and .ReadWrite.All, application roles since 22 September, gained their delegated scopes. Every delegated scope is of type Admin, so each needs admin consent; all are enabled, none is in the permissions reference, and all nine names had been in Microsoft's deployment map since September or earlier. The same dump carries the new display text of EntraBackup.Read.All, 'Read Entra Backup configuration, preview jobs, and snapshots'. One read holds the names; on 5 and 6 October consecutive dumps disagreed for a day, so treat this as rolling out until a second dump confirms it.
items.why: AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All lets an app 'create, read, update, and delete the trusted federated credential issuers that can be used to restrict which identity providers must be used when configuring federated identity credentials', without a signed-in user: whoever holds it decides which external identity providers a workload identity in the tenant may trust. CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All can create and delete Copilot spending policies that, in Microsoft's words, 'may take effect immediately and restrict user spending', and CopilotCostManagement-UserData.Read.All reads 'any named user's Copilot credit balance' and usage by security group. Microsoft has published no documentation for any of the three families.
items.action: Nothing is granted by this change. Add the two application role IDs and nine delegated scope IDs from the Graph API tab to the consent watch list today, decline consent for AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All until Microsoft documents the feature, and run the first query in Hunting & actions to confirm none has been granted since 6 October.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft: beginning 1 April 2027 selected Microsoft Graph file APIs no longer return pre-authenticated URLs; the service change runs early to late April 2027. Message Center prints 1 April 2027 as the act-by date.
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Graph: New tenant controls for retirement of non-standard file API tokens
items.title: Pre-authenticated (tempauth) file URLs retire on 1 April 2027: Graph file APIs stop returning URLs with an embedded token, and a tenant control lets you test per application first
items.fingerprint: Microsoft is retiring pre-authenticated URLs, also known as tempauth URLs, from SharePoint Online and OneDrive. 'Beginning April 1, 2027, selected Microsoft Graph file APIs will no longer return URLs that contain embedded authentication information and will no longer issue HTTP 302 redirects to those URLs.' Affected families: file download and content, createUploadSession, copy and long-running action monitors, preview, thumbnail, version and format conversion. New SharePoint Online tenant controls, coming in a future release of the SharePoint Online PowerShell module (Get- and Clear-SPOTenantPreAuthSettings are documented), let administrators opt specific application IDs into the new behaviour before the date; the change is not enabled by default through the controls. Requests made directly to SharePoint APIs are not affected by the tenant setting. Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD, early to late April 2027.
items.why: A tempauth URL is a bearer credential in a link: whoever holds the URL reads the file with no further authentication for as long as it lives, and it travels through logs, proxies and tickets. Its retirement removes that exposure, and it also breaks every backup tool, migration tool, scanner and line-of-business script that stores, inspects or redeems such URLs or follows the 302 redirect. Applications that call SharePoint URLs directly afterwards need an Entra ID access token for the SharePoint resource, which also means their file access appears in sign-in logs where it did not before.
items.action: Ask the owners of backup, DLP, eDiscovery, migration and custom integrations whether they use Graph download, upload-session, copy, preview, thumbnail or version URLs; when the tenant control ships, opt a small set of application IDs in and watch for authentication failures before widening it. Record the vendors' support dates well before April 2027.

items.publishedNote: Dated from commit 4315a4c603 in MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs, 20:55 Warsaw on 9 October 2026, which added the article; the page's own ms.date is 6 October 2026. The published Learn page was read through the Microsoft Learn MCP server in this run.
items.officialTitle: Entra Agent ID lifecycle policies (preview)
items.title: Agent ID lifecycle policies (preview): Lifecycle Workflows can disable or delete agent identities that are inactive, have too few sponsors or were not reconfirmed
items.fingerprint: A new how-to article under ID Governance, Lifecycle Workflows, Lifecycle Policies, Agent IDs. A policy scopes a set of agent identities and enables one or more of three rules: periodic reconfirmation by a sponsor or owner (every 30 to 730 days), a minimum number of sponsors, and inactivity monitoring, where inactive means 'no tokens have been issued for the identity during that time'. The policy action is Disable, Delete (a soft delete) or Disable and delete after a configurable number of days, with an optional grace period; sponsors, owners or a fallback recipient are notified first, and 'If the violation isn't remediated within the configured timeframe, Lifecycle Workflows automatically executes the policy action.' Where policies overlap, 'The highest-priority matching policy applies to the agent identity.' Roles: Lifecycle Workflows Administrator or AI Administrator. Licence: Microsoft 365 E7, or Microsoft Agent 365 with at least Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3. Preview, with no service-level agreement.
items.why: This is the first Microsoft control that removes an agent identity nobody answers for, which is the population incident responders keep finding with standing access. It is also a new way for an identity to be disabled or deleted without an administrator doing it by hand: a production agent whose sponsor ignores a notification stops working, and the actor in the audit trail is the lifecycle service. The two LifecyclePolicies-AgentId Graph permissions Microsoft documented on 8 October are the programmatic side of the same feature.
items.action: Pilot with Specific agents as the scope and a fallback recipient the SOC can read, as the article itself recommends, before any tenant-wide policy; decide who may hold Lifecycle Workflows Administrator and AI Administrator, because either can now schedule deletion of agent identities.

items.title: Search-UnifiedAuditLog retires on 15 October 2027; the Graph AuditLogQuery API is generally available now and replaces it
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview Audit: AuditLogQuery API generally available and Search-UnifiedAuditLog retiring
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states 'On October 15, 2027, Search-UnifiedAuditLog will be retired and will no longer provide access to the audit log.'
items.fingerprint: Message Center MC1505599, published 12 October 2026: the Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API (/security/auditLog/queries) is generally available worldwide from early October 2026, with workload-scoped permissions (AuditLogsQuery-Entra/-Exchange/-SharePoint/-OneDrive/-Endpoint/-CRM.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery.Read.All), up to 1 million records per query and tenant throttling of 200 search submissions per rolling 24 hours and 50 queued or running. Search-UnifiedAuditLog keeps working unchanged until 15 October 2027 and then no longer returns the audit log; there is no tenant setting to prevent the retirement.
items.why: Every SOC script, SOAR playbook and SIEM pull that calls Search-UnifiedAuditLog stops returning audit data on 15 October 2027. The replacement is asynchronous, throttled at 200 searches a day per tenant, and grants audit reach per workload through new Graph application permissions, so an app holding AuditLogsQuery.Read.All can read the audit log of every service.
items.action: Inventory every script, runbook and connector that calls Search-UnifiedAuditLog; plan the move to POST /security/auditLog/queries with the narrowest AuditLogsQuery-<workload>.Read.All permission; size investigations against the 200-per-day limit; and add the AuditLogsQuery permissions to the app-consent review list.

items.title: App Builder agent and vibe.powerapps.com retire on 30 November 2026; new app creation stops mid-October
items.officialTitle: Microsoft 365 Copilot and Power Apps: Retirement of App Builder agent and vibe.powerapps.com
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states 'On November 30, 2026, the App Builder agent and vibe.powerapps.com will be retired.' actionRequiredByDateTime is 30 November 2026.
items.fingerprint: Message Center MC1505609, published 12 October 2026: Microsoft retires the App Builder agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot and vibe.powerapps.com on 30 November 2026. From mid-October 2026 new apps can no longer be created there and in-product migration becomes available; apps not migrated by 30 November are no longer accessible through these experiences. Copilot Cowork (Frontier) and Microsoft Copilot Studio become the app-building experiences.
items.why: Apps built by makers in these two experiences hold data connections; migrating them into Copilot Studio or Copilot Cowork changes where they run and who owns them, and an app that is not migrated silently stops being reachable.
items.action: Identify makers using App Builder or vibe.powerapps.com, tell them about the 30 November date, and review the migrated apps' connections and sharing in Copilot Studio as they move.

items.title: Universal Continuous Access Evaluation in Global Secure Access now acts on user-risk and device-revocation signals (deleted, disabled or noncompliant device)
items.officialTitle: What's new in Microsoft Entra: October 2026
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Entra blog 'What's new in Microsoft Entra: October 2026', 12 October 2026: Universal Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) in Global Secure Access 'now supports user-risk and device-revocation signals, including when a device is deleted, disabled, or becomes noncompliant.' Public Preview.
items.why: A device the SOC disables or deletes during containment, or one that falls out of compliance, can now end an active Global Secure Access session instead of waiting for token expiry.
items.action: In a pilot, disable a test device and measure how fast its Global Secure Access session is revoked; add that step to the device-containment runbook once it holds.

items.title: Service-to-service token binding: mTLS proof of possession binds Entra access tokens to the managed-identity workload that requested them
items.officialTitle: What's new in Microsoft Entra: October 2026
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Entra blog, 12 October 2026: service-to-service token binding 'uses mutual TLS proof of possession (mTLS PoP) to cryptographically bind an access token to the originating workload.' The initial release supports managed identity workloads on Trusted Launch or Confidential VM / VM Scale Sets using the latest compatible .NET libraries to access Azure Key Vault. General Availability.
items.why: A token stolen from a bound workload can no longer be replayed from elsewhere against Key Vault, which closes the token-theft path that managed identities on compromised VMs offer.
items.action: Identify managed identities on Trusted Launch or Confidential VMs that read Key Vault secrets and enable binding for them cohort by cohort, validating in preproduction first as Microsoft advises.

items.tier0Note: Touches the directory synchronization host and its service accounts, which write into AD DS and Entra ID.
items.title: Guided migration tool from Entra Connect Sync to Cloud Sync is generally available
items.officialTitle: What's new in Microsoft Entra: October 2026
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Entra blog, 12 October 2026: 'The guided migration tool gives eligible organizations a structured path from Microsoft Entra Connect Sync to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync', covering readiness assessment, provisioning agent and Cloud Sync configuration, activation through a controlled transition and post-activation validation. General Availability. Revised 21 October 2026 (entra-docs dd15f12): the guided tool must be started on the ACTIVE Connect Sync server, never one in staging mode; device synchronization is a migration blocker for the guided tool; a ‘Migration blocked’ readiness result must not be bypassed; the tool’s Total Objects check does not validate individual users and groups, memberships, password hash sync, password writeback or Exchange hybrid writeback, which must be checked by hand.
items.why: Moving synchronization to Cloud Sync replaces the Connect Sync server, a tier-0 host, with lightweight provisioning agents and a gMSA, and changes which logs and accounts the SOC watches for sync tampering.
items.action: Before running the tool, list the Connect Sync server, its service accounts and its alerts; after activation, move monitoring to the provisioning agents, their gMSA and the provisioning logs, and decommission the old server deliberately. Add the four manual validations Microsoft now lists to the cut-over checklist.

items.tier0Note: HR inbound provisioning writes user objects into AD DS and Entra ID.
items.title: SAP SuccessFactors provisioning can use workload-identity authentication ahead of SAP's November 2026 basic-auth deprecation
items.officialTitle: What's new in Microsoft Entra: October 2026
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Entra blog, 12 October 2026: Entra supports Workload Identity-based authentication for SAP SuccessFactors provisioning, 'replacing long-lived usernames and passwords with Entra-managed credentials and short-lived, standards-based access tokens', upgradeable in place on existing jobs, 'ahead of SAP SuccessFactors' planned deprecation of basic authentication for its APIs in November 2026.' Public Preview.
items.why: The HR-driven provisioning job creates and enables accounts in AD and Entra ID; its stored SuccessFactors password is a long-lived secret that SAP will stop accepting in November 2026.
items.action: Find SuccessFactors inbound provisioning jobs still on basic authentication and plan the in-place switch before SAP's November 2026 deprecation; Microsoft states no date for general availability.

items.title: TLS inspection in Global Secure Access can use Microsoft-managed certificates instead of a customer certificate authority
items.officialTitle: What's new in Microsoft Entra: October 2026
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Entra blog, 12 October 2026: 'With Microsoft-managed certificates, Microsoft provisions the inspection certificate, removing the need for customers to operate their own certificate authority or public key infrastructure to use TLS inspection.' Public Preview.
items.why: TLS inspection becomes easier to switch on, so more decrypted web traffic reaches GSA logs and DLP; the trust anchor for that interception moves to Microsoft, which device trust stores must accept.
items.action: If you pilot it, record which root the inspection certificate chains to, how it reaches device trust stores, and which destinations are excluded from inspection.

items.title: Security Operator is now documented as able to disable, enable, revoke sessions and force a password change on Entra ID accounts from Defender for Identity
items.officialTitle: Remediation Actions for Compromised Users in Microsoft Defender for Identity
items.fingerprintBefore: Microsoft Entra ID column, Disable: Global Administrator, User Administrator, Authentication Administrator, Privileged Authentication Administrator, Directory Writers, SOC Identity Responder
items.fingerprint: Defender for Identity 'Remediation actions' page, Roles and permissions table, revised 12 October 2026 (read from the merill/defender-docs-mirror commit 41e4ba6): the Microsoft Entra ID column for Disable, Enable, Revoke session and Force password change now ends with 'SOC Identity Responder, Security Operator'; Security Operator was previously listed only for Mark as compromised.
items.why: Security Operator is a common SOC analyst role. If the page reflects the service, holders of it can now disable an Entra ID account, revoke its sessions or force its password change from the identity page in Defender XDR, which is a containment power and also a way to lock out an administrator.
items.action: List Security Operator assignments (including PIM-eligible) and confirm each holder should be able to disable accounts and force password changes; alert on these remediation actions in the Defender XDR action center and the Entra audit log when performed by a Security Operator.

items.title: Entra stops auto-granting AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprints from 4 November; app-only agents that create their own identities need explicit admin consent or get 403
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra: Changes to AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission for agent identities
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft names 4 November as the start; rollout runs early to late November 2026
items.fingerprint: Starting 4 November 2026 Microsoft Entra no longer automatically grants the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission to agent blueprint principals; an administrator must grant it through tenant-wide admin consent or an app-role assignment, which Microsoft says is possible from 16 October and fails if attempted earlier. An app-only request that relies on the automatic grant after enforcement fails with 403. Existing agent identities and blueprints are not removed, and agents authorised through a directory role are not affected.
items.why: Until now every agent blueprint could mint agent identities without any admin approval and without a visible grant. After the change that authority becomes an auditable, revocable app-role assignment, so the grant itself becomes something to monitor.
items.action: Before 4 November, filter the Entra audit log on ApplicationManagement / Add Service Principal where the initiator is an Application and the target an agent identity; grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager explicitly (from 16 October) only to the blueprints that need it, and alert on new grants of it afterwards.

items.title: From 4 November every default user can create agent blueprints unless 'Users can create agent blueprints' is set to No
items.officialTitle: Action may be required: Review who can create agents in Microsoft Entra
items.deadlineNote: Rollout begins early November (Microsoft names 4 November) and completes late November 2026
items.fingerprint: Starting 4 November 2026 users without any built-in or custom Entra role can create new agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off the new user setting 'Users can create agent blueprints' under Default user role permissions. The setting can be changed now and takes effect when rollout begins. It is independent of 'Users can register applications'; it does not change existing blueprints or who can create identities from them.
items.why: A default-on permission for every member user to create a new kind of workload identity widens the app-registration surface that consent-phishing and persistence techniques already abuse, and tenants that locked down app registration are not covered by that setting.
items.action: Decide before 4 November: set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No unless there is a business case, keep Agent ID Developer as the delegated path, and add agent blueprint creation by non-admins to the app-registration detections.

items.title: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors: completion moves from late November to mid-December 2026
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
items.deadlineNote: Rollout began early October 2026 and is expected to complete mid-December 2026; no calendar date
items.fingerprintBefore: General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete in late November 2026
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised MC1450134 on 13 October 2026 ('We have updated the timeline'): rollout began early October 2026 and is now expected to complete in mid-December 2026 (previously late November). After rollout WHfB and macOS PSSO satisfy step-up MFA, Authentication Strength and sign-in frequency challenges on their own, users whose only MFA method is WHfB or PSSO count as MFA-capable, and password-only users with WHfB or PSSO are no longer prompted to register another method.
items.why: A device-bound credential becomes enough to count a user as MFA-capable, so MFA registration reports and the 'users without MFA' hunting queries change meaning while rollout is in progress, and users can be left without any portable method.
items.action: Require a second, portable method (synced or Authenticator passkey) in onboarding, re-check custom Authentication Strengths, and annotate MFA-coverage reports for the rollout period.

items.title: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening is now in enforcement with the October Windows security update
items.officialTitle: AD FS Distributed Key Manager (DKM) container ACL hardening begins today
items.deadlineNote: Enforcement started with the 13 October 2026 update; tracked in MC1456735 and MC1471963
items.tier0Note: It changes the ACLs on the AD DS container holding the AD FS token-signing key material.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft confirmed on 13 October 2026 that AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening (CVE-2026-56155) begins with the October 2026 Windows security update, the enforcement step announced in MC1456735 and MC1471963.
items.why: The hardened ACLs protect the key material that signs federation tokens; a server that was not remediated, or a Windows Server 2012/2012 R2 host that never is, stays exposed.
items.action: After patching, check the AD FS Admin log for Event ID 1132 on every federation server and remediate Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 by hand.

items.title: Windows 11 security baselines turn Administrator protection on by default from the October update
items.officialTitle: Manage Administrator protection within Windows 11 security baseline
items.fingerprint: With the October 2026 Windows security update the Windows 11 security baselines for 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2 enable Administrator protection by default through two UAC policies (Configure type of Admin Approval Mode; Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators running with Administrator protection). The feature itself stays generally available and off by default outside the baseline.
items.why: Administrator protection replaces the admin's standing elevated token with just-in-time elevation through a separate system-managed account, which changes how local-admin elevation appears in endpoint telemetry and can break scripts and tools that expect silent elevation.
items.action: Test the baseline on a pilot ring, decide the two UAC policies explicitly in Intune or Group Policy, and re-baseline any detections keyed on elevation events.

items.title: ReFS on removable media: audit from the October update, blocking by default from the January 2027 update
items.officialTitle: Hardening changes for ReFS volumes on removable media
items.deadlineNote: Enforcement with the January 2027 Windows security update; Microsoft gives no calendar date
items.fingerprint: Microsoft is hardening the Resilient File System: the October 2026 Windows security update adds audit events for ReFS volumes in unsupported external (removable media) configurations and controls to block them; with the January 2027 security update blocking becomes the default unless an override is configured.
items.why: Removable-media ReFS is an unsupported parsing surface; the audit events are new endpoint telemetry worth collecting, and the January default will block any workflow still relying on it.
items.action: Collect the new ReFS audit events, find workflows that depend on ReFS removable media, and test blocking before January.

items.title: The October 2026 Windows security update is available

items.why: Offline compliance scans run against the September cab will report October-patched machines as compliant with an older baseline, and October missing patches will not show.
items.action: Do not treat offline Scan Cab compliance reports as current for October until Microsoft publishes the cab.

items.title: Purview RBAC audit: two new operations, and role-group and permission-assignment records now say which portal made the change
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft Purview: permissions audit log improvements
items.deadlineNote: Rollout late September to late October 2026
items.fingerprintBefore: New audit operations CheckUsersInRoles and CheckUserInRolesWithScopes; no portal attribution
items.fingerprint: Microsoft revised MC1473155 on 13 October 2026: besides the two new SecurityComplianceRBAC audit operations CheckUsersInRoles and CheckUserInRolesWithScopes, supported permission-assignment and role-group change records now carry a ClientPortal field inside PreExecutionMessage with the value 'Microsoft Purview', 'Microsoft Defender' or 'Unknown'.
items.why: Role-group changes in Purview and Defender land in the same audit stream; the ClientPortal field lets a detection tell which portal an RBAC change came from.
items.action: Add ClientPortal to parsers for SecurityComplianceRBAC records and include the two new operations in RBAC change monitoring.

items.why: Every tenant gains an agent inventory with usage data, which is the starting point for finding unsanctioned agents.
items.action: Once it reaches the tenant, review the Registry for agents nobody owns.

items.title: Copilot Studio retires GPT-4.1, GPT-5 Chat/Auto/Reasoning and GPT 5.6 Sol/Luna on 12 November and migrates agents automatically

items.title: Windows Server 2022 left mainstream support on 13 October; security updates continue to 14 October 2031
items.officialTitle: Windows Server 2022 has reached end of mainstream support
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft writes: “As of October 13, 2026, Windows Server 2022 has reached end of mainstream support and transitioned to extended support.”
items.fingerprint: Windows Server 2022 reached end of mainstream support on 13 October 2026 and moved to extended support; the October 2026 security update is the last mainstream update, monthly security updates continue at no extra cost through 14 October 2031, and hotpatch for Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition is extended through October 2027.
items.why: Security fixes continue, but non-security fixes and feature work stop; a defect found on a 2022 domain controller or AD FS host from now on is fixed only if it is a security issue.
items.action: Record Windows Server 2022 as extended-support in the asset inventory and put 2022 domain controllers and tier-0 hosts on the Windows Server 2025 upgrade plan; nothing breaks today.

items.tier0Note: Windows Server 2016 is still a common domain controller and AD FS operating system: an unpatched DC is a direct write path into AD DS.
items.title: Windows Server 2016 gets its last security update in January 2027 (90-day reminder); Essentials features end the same day
items.officialTitle: 90-Day Reminder: Windows Server 2016 will reach end of updates on January 12, 2027
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft writes: “On January 12, 2027, Windows Server 2016 will reach end of updates. The January 2027 Windows security update will be the last update available for this version.”
items.fingerprint: On 12 January 2027 every edition of Windows Server 2016 (Datacenter, Essentials, MultiPoint Premium, Standard) reaches end of updates; the January 2027 security update is the last one. Support for Windows Server 2016 Essentials features such as Remote Web Access ends the same day. Extended Security Updates are available for Standard and Datacenter.
items.why: Domain controllers, AD FS, Exchange and CA servers on 2016 stop receiving security fixes in 89 days unless they are on ESU; the first post-January vulnerability in Kerberos or Netlogon would be unpatched on them.
items.action: List every Windows Server 2016 host by role (DC, AD FS, CA, Entra Connect, Exchange), decide per host between upgrade to 2025 and an ESU purchase, and start with tier-0 roles.

items.title: Teams meeting options will offer only the automatic recording and transcription choices the organizer's policy allows, and add 'Record only'

items.action: Check which meeting policies allow recording but block transcription; tell organizers about 'Record only' if transcripts are relied on for retention.

items.title: Teams will flag phishing and social engineering in external first-contact chats with AI-based detection (roadmap, November 2026)

items.why: External Teams chat is a live initial-access channel (help-desk impersonation, fake IT support); a native warning changes what users report and what Defender sees.
items.action: When it reaches Targeted Release, check whether the detections surface in Defender XDR as alerts or only as user warnings, and update the help-desk impersonation playbook accordingly.

items.title: Teams will detect malicious QR codes in messages in near real time (roadmap, December 2026, government clouds)
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Teams: Near-real-time detection of malicious QR codes in messages
items.fingerprint: Microsoft 365 Roadmap 576198, created 14 October 2026, in development for December CY2026 GA in GCC, GCC High and DoD: Teams analyses destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages and extends existing URL protection to QR-based phishing. On 16 October 2026 the roadmap narrowed its cloud instances to Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only; GCC, GCC High and DoD were removed.

items.action: Government-cloud tenants: note the date; commercial tenants: the roadmap entry lists no Worldwide instance.
items.revisionNote: DeltaPulse change record of 17 October 2026 00:00 UTC: cloud instances narrowed from Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD to Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only.

items.title: Purview server-side auto-labeling will cover legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files in SharePoint and OneDrive (roadmap, November 2026)

items.fingerprint: Reminder to Entra ID P2 tenants: the Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users', created in report-only mode with its own security group, ends its 30-day evaluation the week of 28 October 2026 and is automatically switched On unless an admin sets it On or Off first. When On, users at high user risk are prompted to self-remediate through adaptive risk remediation; existing CA settings and exclusions such as break-glass accounts are not altered. The index notes the post has so far been seen only in Education tenants.

items.fingerprint: From mid-November to late November 2026 (GA, Worldwide) published Purview sensitivity labels can be applied to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups at or after creation through the Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell or Microsoft Graph, enforcing membership and guest-access policy; once applied a label cannot currently be changed or removed, and the tenant configuration is separate from the Microsoft 365 groups one. Roadmap 568217.
items.why: Security groups gate access to apps and resources; a label that sets guest access and cannot be removed is a one-way change on objects that Conditional Access and app assignments depend on.
items.action: Before labelling any security group, test on a throw-away group, decide which groups may carry a label, and restrict who can apply labels to groups.

items.fingerprint: A new Exchange Online DLP condition, 'Count of labeled documents is greater than', counts sensitivity-labeled attachments in one message (duplicates included, strict greater-than) and triggers DLP actions above a threshold; public preview early November to early December 2026, GA mid to late December 2026. It does not apply to SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams or Endpoint DLP. Roadmap 562342.
items.why: Bulk sending of labeled files is a classic exfiltration pattern; a volume condition gives a DLP signal that content matching alone misses.
items.action: Plan a test rule in simulation mode with a threshold based on normal business volume once the preview reaches the tenant.

Among the Critical ones: Windows Active Directory Domain Services RCE CVE-2026-70229 (CVSS 8.1, exploitation more likely), Microsoft Exchange Server RCE CVE-2026-70571 (8.1, more likely), AD FS spoofing CVE-2026-108131 (7.5) and NDES RCE CVE-2026-69802 (8.1).
