components.name: Entra Connect Sync
components.deadlineNote: Synchronization stops on any server below the version whose support ends on this date.

items.text: This release includes security fixes. We recommend upgrading to this version as soon as possible.
09/23/2026: Released for download via the Microsoft Entra admin center. This is a hotfix release.

Fixed an issue in version 2.6.91.0 where enabling Pass-through Authentication through the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard could fail while registering the locally installed Microsoft Entra Connect Authentication Agent.
This release includes security fixes. We recommend upgrading to this version as soon as possible.

Added a guided migration workflow from Microsoft Entra Connect Sync to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. The workflow includes configuration assessment, provisioning agent setup, staged activation, and validation. This feature is available only in the Azure public cloud.
Added support for an additional sovereign cloud environment, including Pass-through Authentication, Seamless Single Sign-On, password writeback, and Health Agent monitoring.

Phishing-resistant authentication in the Microsoft Entra Connect setup wizard is now generally available and enabled by default. The Windows Web Account Manager prompt supports passkeys, FIDO2 security keys, and passwords, reuses the signed-in session across Microsoft Entra services, and preserves Seamless Single Sign-On Kerberos key rotation.

Cloud configuration cmdlets no longer require an explicit -AADUserName. When you omit the parameter, Microsoft Entra Connect derives a sign-in hint from the connector configuration and opens an interactive sign-in prompt. This behavior applies to Set-ADSyncAADCompanyFeature, Set-ADSyncAADPasswordSyncState, Enable-ADSyncExportDeletionThreshold, Set-ADSyncScheduler, and Set-ADSyncDirSyncConfiguration.

The Select Containers dialog in Synchronization Service Manager is now read-only. You can still use the dialog to view the current selections. To make changes, use Customize synchronization options in the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard.
When you configure Seamless Single Sign-On by using the standalone PowerShell module, you must import ADSync.psd1 before AzureADSSO.psd1.
Updated the bundled SQL Server 2022 LocalDB from version 16.0.4250.1 to 16.0.4262.2.
Fixed an Application-Based Authentication certificate rotation issue that could remove the last usable application key during directory replica delays.

Fixed an issue where expanding a previously deselected domain on the Domain and OU filtering page could reselect the domain and enable synchronization for the entire domain after the wizard completed.
Fixed multiple security vulnerabilities in bundled third-party dependencies and hardened local temporary-file permissions and SharePoint connector profile-image downloads.

Microsoft Graph permissions have been added to Microsoft Entra Connect. If you use app-scoped Conditional Access policies, review policies targeting Microsoft.Azure.SyncFabric or Microsoft 365 Reporting Service.
Fixed an issue where installing or upgrading Microsoft Entra Connect with an existing ADSync database could fail with error 0xE0474352.
Fixed an issue where upgrading Microsoft Entra Connect didn't update an installed Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable version earlier than 14.41.
Fixed an issue where the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard could close during startup when the Windows PowerShell Transcription policy contained an invalid output directory.
Fixed an issue where Synchronization Service Manager could close unexpectedly when you opened Connector Properties and listed directory partitions.
Fixed an issue where Change Credentials didn't open for connector rows outside the visible area on configurations with many Active Directory connectors.

Enabling Pass-through Authentication through the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard might fail while registering the locally installed Microsoft Entra Connect Authentication Agent. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.92.0.

add: ## Intermittent failures in the SAP logging pipeline

Brief network interruptions, SAP system downtime, or temporary resource constraints can cause a collection request to fail. The agentless data connector automatically retries failed collection windows, so a failed request doesn't immediately mean that logs are permanently lost.
The Microsoft Sentinel poller uses the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) to request logs for collection windows bounded by `startTimeUTC` and `endTimeUTC`. When a window fails:

- The poller retries the same `startTimeUTC` and `endTimeUTC` window according to the configured request retry count. If those retries fail, the poller waits before attempting the same window again. This delay is called backoff.
- Checkpoint advancement occurs only after successful ingestion. A failed window isn't marked as successfully ingested.

If an HTTP connection times out and the poller doesn't receive a successful response, the poller retries the same collection window using the request retry count and backoff described in Automatic retries and checkpoints. Review SAP Cloud Integration message processing logs to diagnose the failure.

rem: ### Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO at first-factor sign-in

Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO are device-bound passkeys that work only as a first factor. Because the **Microsoft managed** state applies system-preferred authentication at the first factor, these credentials can be offered before the password.

To avoid prompting users for a device-bound credential that they don't use or can't complete on their current device, system-preferred authentication offers Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO at the first factor only when the user most recently signed in with a passkey. The behavior de

- If the user has a passkey other than Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO, system-preferred authentication prompts for the passkey at the first factor, just as it already prompts for that passkey at second-factor sign-in.

- If the user's only registered passkey is Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO, and the user most recently signed in with a passkey, system-preferred authentication prompts for passkey sign-in at the first factor.

- If the user's only registered passkey is Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO, and the user's most recent sign-in wasn't with a passkey, system-preferred authentication skips it at the first factor and prompts the next highest-ranked method in the user's credential order instead.

add: ## Supported threat scenarios for real-time protection

Real-time protection inspects agent interactions for threats. When you enable a blocking rule for a threat scenario, interactions that match that scenario are blocked at the intervention point where the threat is detected.

Malicious content propagation occurs when an agent receives, generates, or passes along content identified as malicious. For example, an attacker might include a malicious URL in a user request or tool response, which the agent could then share with a user or pass to another tool.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams: New centralized experience for organizing important resources in chats and channels

entries.title: Microsoft Purview: Archive SharePoint files under retention policies
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management will enable admins to archive inactive SharePoint files under retention policies starting December 2026. Archived files move to Microsoft 365 Archive, remain compliant and discoverable, and are excluded from Copilot indexing, improving response relevance. This feature requires admin configuration.

entries.feedSummary: Microsoft is retiring Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online by April 2027 and expanding Microsoft Graph API support for archive mailboxes. Organizations must migrate applications from EWS to Microsoft Graph APIs by October 2026 to maintain archive mailbox access, compliance, eDiscovery, and data lifecycle management.

entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Teams is enhancing presenter visibility in "Manage what attendees see" by allowing event organizers and producers to drag and resize the presenter panel, displaying more presenters simultaneously. This update, rolling out from mid-August to October 2026, improves event production efficiency without requiring admin action.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams: External presenters can manage event production controls
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Teams now allows event organizers to grant production control permissions to trusted external presenters, including federated (B2B) and guest users, enabling them to manage event production controls. entries.title: Microsoft Teams: Granular channel notification settings
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Teams will introduce granular channel notification presets—All new messages, Mentions and replies, and Mute—with further customization options. Rollout occurs from October to December 2026 across environments. The feature is enabled by default, requires no admin changes, and aims to improve notification control and reduce noise.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams: Breakout rooms now supported in meetings with up to 1,000 attendees
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Teams now supports breakout rooms in meetings with up to 1,000 attendees, allowing up to 100 breakout rooms per meeting. Rollout begins July 2026, with general availability by October 2026. The feature is enabled by default, requires no action, and maintains the existing experience for smaller meetings.

entries.title: Microsoft Purview | Data Lifecycle Management - Archive SharePoint files under retention
entries.feedSummary: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management will enable archiving SharePoint files based on retention policies to reduce storage costs while maintaining compliance. delta.change: Phase 1 rollout window: <del>late October 2026 to late November 2026</del> → <ins>early November 2026 to early January 2027</ins>
delta.impact: A password-only user will be able to register a passkey with no earlier MFA method on the account. Microsoft's own recommendation in the post is to 'Consider requiring MFA to register security information if additional verification is required by your organization.' The change now reaches tenants about three weeks later than this page said.
delta.title: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first MFA method; phase 1 now starts early November and ends early January

delta.change: GPT Chat Latest wording: <del>It keeps agents on the latest supported GPT chat model as snapshots within the current major model version are updated over time. Moving to a new major model version is a separate change</del> → <ins>It keeps agents on the latest supported GPT chat model. Moving to a new model version is a separate change</ins>
delta.impact: An automatic model swap changes agent behaviour, including how it handles tool calls and grounding, without an owner approving it.
delta.title: Copilot Studio retires GPT-4.1, GPT-5 Chat/Auto/Reasoning and GPT 5.6 Sol/Luna on 12 November and migrates agents automatically

delta.change: <ins>MSRC (26 October 2026): eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys (six TLS, two code signing) were compromised in eMudhra's hierarchy, not at Microsoft. 20 October: the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List blocks the affected CAs; Edge and WebView2 block the TLS certificates through CRLSet. 26 October: out-of-band Windows updates (KB5134133 for Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H2, KB5134137 for Server 2025, KB5134140 for Server 2022, KB5134123-25 and KB5134130/34 for the rest) remove six eMudhra G3 roots and an AAA Certificate Services cross-sign. 27 October: the same seven leave the Edge trust list.</ins>
delta.impact: A certificate that chains to a compromised CA can impersonate a TLS endpoint or sign code that Windows trusts; disconnected or WSUS-only devices that never received the 20 October Disallowed list still trust it.
delta.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys compromised: Windows blocked the CAs on 20 October, an out-of-band update removes seven eMudhra roots on 26 October and Edge follows on 27 October

delta.change: <ins>First read today; Microsoft revised it on 26 October 2026</ins>: Revised 26 October 2026: GA rollout began late September and now completes by mid-November 2026 (previously mid-October). The MessageContents table exposes Teams message snippets and metadata, including messages with URLs and federated messages, to analysts holding the Advanced Hunting and message preview permissions.
delta.impact: A hunting table that holds Teams message content is a new place where message text is readable; who holds message preview permission decides who can read it.
delta.title: Advanced hunting gains a MessageContents table with Teams message snippets; GA now completes by mid-November, not mid-October

delta.change: <ins>GA begins early November and completes mid-November 2026. Teams decodes QR codes in inline images in 1:1, group and meeting chats and channels, internal and external, and shows 'This message contains a link that might be harmful' when the destination is malicious. Governed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting (on by default); no separate control.</ins>
delta.impact: QR-code phishing in Teams has had no URL verdict until now; the warning gives users and the help desk a signal, and internal senders, whose QR images are not blurred, are covered too.

watchlist.state: New real-time user risk detection documented on 19 October 2026; riskEventType named on 21 October
watchlist.what: Microsoft: 'This detection identifies when a new authentication method is added to an account under suspicious circumstances.' Calculated in real time, Entra ID P2, riskEventType suspiciousCredentialAddition.
watchlist.soc: Rules that match on a fixed list of riskEventType values will not see it until the list is updated; pair it with AuditLogs security-info registration events.

watchlist.state: General availability on 30 October 2026 confirmed by MC1519855, published 21 October 2026
watchlist.what: Microsoft: from 30 October 2026 organizations can configure a supported third-party telephony provider, chosen through Microsoft Security Store, for SMS and voice authentication; Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retires 1 February 2027 (Global Administrators and external users 1 July 2027), after which users with only SMS or voice get a blocking passkey registration prompt unless a provider is configured.
watchlist.soc: The only path that keeps telephony methods alive puts a third party in the MFA delivery path; count the SMS/voice-only users first and buy a provider only for a documented residue.

watchlist.state: Write access grantable to applications since the 16 October 2026 service principal dump; undocumented
watchlist.what: Microsoft's display text: 'Update certificateUserIds for all users' — 'Allows the app to update certificate user IDs for all users, without a signed-in user.' Application role 10d0f892-6ef8-4cd8-9f4c-614345762e90, delegated scope 01d92422-30dd-4401-a504-aa0a84c463bc, admin consent; not on the permissions reference.
watchlist.soc: certificateUserIds decides which user a certificate signs in as under certificate-based authentication, so a grant of this permission is a grant over sign-in itself (inferred from how CBA user binding works). Alert on the grant and on every certificateUserIds change.

watchlist.topic: Security Defaults managed rule by rule
watchlist.state: Withdrawn from the documentation on 16 October 2026, two days after it appeared
watchlist.what: The section 'Manage individual Security Defaults protections (preview)' is gone from the Security defaults page; the page again describes one set of protections enabled together, including blocking device code flow, and points to Conditional Access for exceptions.
watchlist.soc: Do not plan around per-rule Security Defaults or running them beside Conditional Access; the 14 October text no longer stands.

watchlist.state: Blocked by default from the October 2026 security update where Credential Guard is off
watchlist.what: Microsoft: 'Beginning with the October 2026 security update, Windows uses Enforce mode as the internal default behavior instead of Audit mode, if the registry key BlockNtlmv1SSO has not been previously configured.' Wi-Fi, Ethernet and VPN using PEAP-MSCHAPv2 or EAP-MSCHAPv2 for SSO may fail; BlockNtlmv1SSO = 0 returns to audit (Event ID 4024), 1 enforces (Event ID 4025).
watchlist.soc: The temporary rollback re-opens a credential path Microsoft calls comparable to NTLMv1; every device set to 0 should be a dated exception, and Event ID 4024 tells you whether the dependency is still there.

watchlist.state: Risk-based CAPTCHA before an SMS or call may now be shown; documented 15 October 2026
watchlist.what: Microsoft: users 'might be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step, such as a CAPTCHA, before Microsoft sends an SMS message or places a voice call for sign-in'; the provider is Arkose Labs and Microsoft does not publish the risk criteria.
watchlist.soc: SMS and voice are abused enough for Microsoft to gate them with a bot check. Make sure the Arkose Labs domains are reachable, and keep moving users off telephony methods.

watchlist.state: Documented as Real-time since 15 October 2026 (Offline before)
watchlist.what: The risk detection table now reads 'Atypical travel | Real-time | Premium | unlikelyTravel' and 'Calculated in real-time'; the 14-day or 10-login learning period sentence was replaced by 'adaptive learning'.
watchlist.soc: Sign-in-risk Conditional Access policies can now act on atypical travel during the sign-in. Watch DetectionTimingType in AADUserRiskEvents to see when your tenant's detections move.

watchlist.topic: Trusted issuers for federated identity credentials
watchlist.state: Grantable since the 9 October 2026 service principal dump; undocumented
watchlist.what: The Microsoft Graph service principal now carries AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.Read.All and AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All, each as an application role and a delegated scope. Microsoft's description of the write form: 'Allows the app to create, read, update, and delete the trusted federated credential issuers that can be used to restrict which identity providers must be used when configuring federated identity credentials, without a signed-in user'. Microsoft has published no documentation for the feature.
watchlist.soc: A federated identity credential lets an external token stand in for an application's secret. A tenant list of trusted issuers is the control over which external identity providers may do that, so the permission that writes the list belongs on the consent watch list from the first day it is grantable.

watchlist.state: Documented on 8 October 2026; grantable since August
watchlist.what: Microsoft's permissions reference now carries UserAuthenticationMethod.Delete.All and twelve per-method UserAuthMethod-*.Delete.All application permissions, each with admin consent required. For passkeys: 'Allows the application to delete passkey authentication methods of all users in your organization, without a signed-in user. This does not allow the app to read, create, or modify passkey authentication methods.'
watchlist.soc: Deleting the strong method is how an account is pushed back to a weaker one. These roles grant no read or write, so they hide from reviews that search for ReadWrite; alert on any grant of the thirteen identifiers.

watchlist.topic: Authenticated password change in My Sign-Ins
watchlist.state: Schedule revised by Microsoft on 9 October 2026; off by default
watchlist.what: MC1437671, revised 9 October 2026: general availability, Worldwide and GCC, now begins at the 'end of October 2026 (previously mid-October)' and is 'expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)'. A user with a passkey, FIDO2 security key or Windows Hello for Business can set a new password from My Sign-Ins without knowing the current one and without SSPR. 'There is no per-user or per-group scoping.'
watchlist.soc: One strong credential becomes enough to replace the password on the same account, for every user or for none. Decide before the switch appears, and watch password changes that follow a fresh passkey registration.

watchlist.topic: System-preferred authentication and the registration campaign
watchlist.what: Microsoft removed the note that the Microsoft managed state 'affects both first-factor and multifactor authentication and is being gradually deployed to tenants through September 2026', and the note that the new registration campaign 'is expected to finish by the end of September 2026'. The commit is titled 'Remove completed system-preferred rollout note'.
watchlist.soc: Both behaviours are now documented as every tenant's. A tenant that does not show them has a configuration difference worth finding, not a rollout to wait for.

watchlist.what: Microsoft's own version-history page states that all synchronisation services in Entra Connect Sync stop working on 30 September 2026 for any server below 2.5.79.0. The current build is 2.6.92.0, released 23 September 2026 as a hotfix for a Pass-through Authentication agent registration failure introduced in 2.6.91.0; 2.6.91.0 itself, on 16 September, made phishing-resistant authentication generally available and on by default.
watchlist.soc: If a Connect server is below 2.5.79.0 on 1 October, hybrid identity stops syncing: no new accounts, no disables, no group changes. A leaver who is disabled on-premises stays enabled in the cloud. That is the failure mode to plan for, not the sync alert.

watchlist.what: Three beta properties on security/auditLogQuery - isRecordCountLimitExceeded, recordCountLimit and approximateReturnedRecordCount - say whether a completed query hit the per-search record limit. Before them, a truncated answer and a quiet day looked identical.
watchlist.soc: Every collector that pages the unified audit log through Graph has been unable to tell the two apart. Read the flag and alert on it; a hunt that silently loses rows is worse than a hunt that fails.

watchlist.what: MC1474104, published 18 September, sets the date: from 1 February 2027 SMS first-factor sign-in is retired for Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenants worldwide and in GCC. Existing configurations stop being honoured and the management surface is removed.
watchlist.soc: Any account that can still sign in with a phone number and an SMS code is a phishable first factor with a February deadline on it. Inventory SignInNoPassword usage now; the population is usually frontline and shared-device users, who are the hardest to move.

watchlist.what: MC1426371, last revised 15 September, is the parent post: passkeys become the default registration path and Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire. Its own first deadline, 1 September 2026, has passed.
watchlist.soc: Tenants that relied on Microsoft-provided telephony have two exits — move to phishing-resistant methods, or bring their own telephony provider — and the provider route has its own dates.

watchlist.topic: Passkeys as the first registered method
watchlist.what: MC1450133 lets a user register a passkey or another passwordless method as their first multifactor method, rather than having to register a phone first.
watchlist.soc: Removes the step that forced every new user through a phone number. It also removes the assumption, common in detection rules, that a first registration event is a phone registration.

watchlist.what: MC1459133 extends passkey registration and sign-in to B2B guest users in the resource tenant.
watchlist.soc: Guest identities have been the weakest link in phishing-resistant rollouts because the home tenant controlled the method. This gives the resource tenant a lever it did not have.

watchlist.topic: System-preferred authentication on the first factor
watchlist.what: System-preferred authentication starts applying to the first factor, not just to multifactor prompts, from 30 September 2026.
watchlist.soc: The method a user is offered first changes without any policy edit on the tenant side. Expect help-desk volume and a shift in the method distribution in sign-in logs at the end of the month.

watchlist.topic: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening
watchlist.what: MC1471963 is the 30-day reminder: the October 2026 Windows security update turns on Enforcement mode for AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening, remediating insecure ACLs automatically to close CVE-2026-56155. Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 are not remediated automatically.
watchlist.soc: This writes to a Tier 0 object on the federation path. Use the remaining audit period to read the AD FS Admin event log and confirm nothing in the tenant depends on the loose ACL.

strategic.head: Vendor multi-tenant apps are now the supply chain an actor walks through
strategic.text: Storm-0940 did not phish a single tenant user: it took over ConnectWise's own multi-tenant apps and signed in app-only wherever those apps already held consent, and one of them gave itself Global Administrator. Storm-3168 in September and Storm-0940 now are two named actors in a month on the same path. A consent granted to a vendor years ago is a standing credential that Conditional Access and MFA do not touch.

strategic.head: Permissions now reach the service principal weeks after the deployment map shows them
strategic.text: On 16 October twelve more names became grantable in the Microsoft Graph service principal, among them UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All and AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All; every one had been in Microsoft's deployment map for weeks (UserCertificateIds since 24 September, the administrative unit trio since March), and none is on the permissions reference. The 5 and 9 October batches followed the same path. A consent review that waits for the documentation is weeks late by design.

strategic.head: The permissions reference catches up in batches, weeks after the service
strategic.text: On 8 October Microsoft documented 33 Graph permissions in one commit; this catalog had held every one of them from the service principal or the deployment map, some since August. A consent process that treats the reference page as the list of what can be granted is weeks behind what can be granted, and one section, Policy.ReadWrite.Recovery, is now ahead of the service instead.

strategic.head: A directory role reaches Graph app role assignments through one Microsoft application
strategic.text: Tenant Governance Administrator is now documented with application-scoped operations, among them managing app role assignments for Microsoft Graph and delegated permission grants. They are written as prose rows, not as microsoft.directory actions, so role-definition scanners do not see them; expect more roles to be documented this way.

strategic.head: The legacy Graph security alerts API fails silently on 15 October
strategic.text: After 15 October /security/alerts returns no data rather than an error, and Microsoft states its replacement is not one-to-one: alerts from a Sentinel workspace that is not connected to the Defender portal do not appear in alerts_v2. An integration can look healthy and be empty.

strategic.head: Exchange Server received an out-of-cycle fix nine days after its September update
strategic.text: CVE-2026-96940 was added on 2 October 2026 as a V2 of the 24 September release, and the WSUS Scan Cab was re-issued the same evening to detect it. A patch process that closes the month once the September update is on will carry this exposure until November unless build numbers are compared.

strategic.head: Two exploited elevation-of-privilege bugs are still being edited three weeks after release
strategic.text: CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880 both carry Exploited: Yes in Microsoft's September document, and both were revised between 14 and 28 September — an acknowledgement on 15 September, an exploit-maturity vector on 16 September. One of them still has no CVSS base score at all. A queue sorted on severity will not show either of them at the top.

strategic.head: Microsoft's own Entra what's-new pages have stopped answering for 16-30 September
strategic.text: All eight official Entra what's-new and breaking-change pages were read in this run and every one of them is stale against a 16-30 September window: the consolidated feed's newest entry is June 2026, identity-platform breaking changes still ends at August 2024. The dated record for Entra in the 16-30 September period comes from Message Center and from the documentation git history, and the Sources tab says so per area.

kql.why: msrc-cve-2026-70197-not-addressed-2026-10-19: Microsoft says the October fix does not address the vulnerability.

Columns from the DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities reference; the table is not ingested into Sentinel. It was not run against a tenant in this pass.

kql.title: Grants of the twelve newly grantable Graph permissions, and every write to certificateUserIds
kql.why: graph-sp-twelve-names-2026-10-16: UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All and AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All became grantable on 16 October 2026.
kql.desc: Finds app role assignments and delegated permission grants whose target carries one of the nineteen new GUIDs read from the 16 October service principal dump, and every Entra audit event whose modified properties name certificateUserIds, with who made the change. The columns are those of the AuditLogs table reference (Log Analytics or Sentinel with Entra audit logs). It was not run against a tenant in this pass.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 17 Oct 2026 - grants of the 16 Oct Graph permissions and certificateUserIds writes
// Log Analytics / Sentinel. Columns as on the AuditLogs table reference cited beside this query. Not run against a tenant in this pass.
let NewGraphIds = dynamic([
  "d2ac92ed-5cdc-4342-8f63-eba03efc5d86","bfe74bc6-06ed-4349-9ba5-6596149bf69a","9205f977-63a7-4c23-9d0c-8051235b0e4c",
  "cb05e9e0-87aa-465c-858a-0c85916c8499","2a3968e7-2e35-4996-92e6-8a44a0e7d56c","e914ccfc-8916-403b-a250-9b8844e9381c",
  "10d0f892-6ef8-4cd8-9f4c-614345762e90",
  "3dcaa6c1-6af2-4d09-8c96-f8f16012d52d","b1c7bc90-edab-4b18-9a7d-441e74635223","14f19140-a110-48da-b3ba-63c2862bb7da",
  "0696c9ff-8589-4687-8015-58a87d0ae29f","29dc273e-f551-4fe3-a672-05bea406787f","c0fcd4f8-e2a8-4162-892c-652d9bb651fd",
  "07bfcf5a-655d-440d-86ed-712989e08b7e","1bc3f48a-9ebf-4bc3-beec-ec63bf290087","8a5e5c26-825e-4065-a444-aa167b44de4b",
  "a9750a17-f46d-45ed-b6b6-42d988745301","f0125870-9fec-449f-8cad-2418f0af0b16","01d92422-30dd-4401-a504-aa0a84c463bc"]);
let NewScopeNames = dynamic(["AdministrativeUnit.ReadBasic.All","AdministrativeUnit.ReadWriteBasic.All","AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All",
  "CrossTenantIdentityMapping.Read.All","CrossTenantIdentityMapping.ReadWrite.All","Policy.Read.SecurityDefaults","UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All",
  "CopilotCostManagement.Read.All","CopilotCostManagement-CreditReq.Read.All","CopilotCostManagement-CreditReq.ReadWrite.All",
  "Repository.Read.All","Repository.ReadWrite.All"]);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Category == "Audit"
| extend Targets = tostring(TargetResources)
| where (OperationName in ("Add app role assignment to service principal", "Add delegated permission grant", "Consent to application")
         and (Targets has_any (NewGraphIds) or Targets has_any (NewScopeNames)))
     or Targets has "certificateUserIds"
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName))
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Result, Actor, Target = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName), Targets
| order by TimeGenerated desc

kql.title: Atypical travel detections by timing type: when does your tenant start seeing them in real time
kql.why: entra-atypical-travel-realtime-2026-10-15: Microsoft now documents atypical travel (unlikelyTravel) as a real-time detection instead of offline.
kql.desc: Counts unlikelyTravel risk detections per day and DetectionTimingType over 30 days, with how many were remediated or dismissed. A shift from offline to realtime shows the change reaching your tenant; a rise in atRisk realtime rows tells you sign-in-risk policies are now challenging these sign-ins. The columns are those of the AADUserRiskEvents table reference (Log Analytics or Sentinel with the Entra ID Protection diagnostic setting). It was not run against a tenant in this pass.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 16 Oct 2026 - atypical travel (unlikelyTravel) by DetectionTimingType
// Log Analytics / Sentinel. Columns as on the AADUserRiskEvents table reference cited beside this query. Not run against a tenant in this pass.
AADUserRiskEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RiskEventType == "unlikelyTravel"
| summarize arg_max(LastUpdatedDateTime, *) by Id
| summarize Detections = count(),
            AtRisk = countif(RiskState == "atRisk"),
            Remediated = countif(RiskState == "remediated"),
            Dismissed = countif(RiskState == "dismissed"),
            Users = dcount(UserPrincipalName)
          by Day = bin(DetectedDateTime, 1d), DetectionTimingType
| order by Day asc, DetectionTimingType asc

kql.title: Who approved post-delivery email remediation, using the new ApproverUpn column
kql.why: mdo-emailpostdeliveryevents-approverupn-2026-10-15: EmailPostDeliveryEvents now carries ApproverUpn, per the Defender for Office 365 what's new page of 15 October 2026.
kql.desc: Lists manual remediation in the last 14 days by the account that approved it, with the actions and recipients touched. An approver outside the SOC or messaging team, or a burst of approvals from one account, is worth a look. ApproverUpn is read with column_ifexists because the EmailPostDeliveryEvents schema page read on 16 October 2026 does not list it yet; every other column is on that page. It was not run against a tenant in this pass.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 16 Oct 2026 - post-delivery remediation by approver
// Defender XDR advanced hunting. ApproverUpn per the MDO what's new page of 15 Oct 2026; not yet on the schema page, hence column_ifexists. Not run against a tenant in this pass.
EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType == "Manual remediation"
| extend Approver = tostring(column_ifexists("ApproverUpn", ""))
| summarize Actions = count(),
            Recipients = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
            ActionList = make_set(Action, 10),
            Results = make_set(ActionResult, 10),
            Triggers = make_set(ActionTrigger, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by Approver
| order by Actions desc

kql.title: Which devices carry a registry tag, and how it compares with their portal and dynamic tags
kql.why: mde-device-tag-registry-single-tag-2026-10-12: Microsoft now documents that the DeviceTagging registry value holds one tag and is not updated by tags set elsewhere.
kql.desc: Lists, for every device seen in seven days, the tag written through the registry next to the tags set in the portal or API and by dynamic rules. A device whose registry tag differs from its manual tags is one where a registry-reading script gives the wrong answer; MachineGroup shows which RBAC device group the tags placed it in. The columns are those of the DeviceInfo schema page. It was not run against a tenant in this pass.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 13 Oct 2026 - device tags: registry tag against portal and dynamic tags
// Defender XDR advanced hunting. Columns as on the DeviceInfo schema page cited beside this query. Not run against a tenant in this pass.
DeviceInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, DeviceName, MachineGroup, RegistryDeviceTag, DeviceManualTags, DeviceDynamicTags) by DeviceId
| where isnotempty(RegistryDeviceTag) or isnotempty(DeviceManualTags) or isnotempty(DeviceDynamicTags)
| project DeviceName, MachineGroup, RegistryDeviceTag, DeviceManualTags, DeviceDynamicTags
| order by MachineGroup asc, DeviceName asc

kql.title: Which Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters still carry the retiring Key Vault Secrets Provider extension
kql.why: azure-arc-akv-secrets-provider-extension-retirement-2027-10-09: Microsoft retires the Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider extension for Arc-enabled Kubernetes on 9 October 2027.
kql.desc: An Azure Resource Graph query, run in Resource Graph Explorer or with az graph query, that lists every Arc-enabled Kubernetes cluster with the extension type Microsoft's migration guide names, microsoft.azurekeyvaultsecretsprovider. Each row is a cluster that holds a service principal credential for Key Vault and needs a migration plan before the retirement date; an empty result means nothing to migrate. The table, the resource type and the ExtensionType property follow Microsoft's own sample query for Arc-enabled Kubernetes extensions. It was not run against a tenant in this pass, so confirm it returns a known extension in yours first.
kql.schemaLabel: Microsoft Learn — Resource Graph samples for Arc-enabled Kubernetes

kql.title: Who was granted one of the Graph permissions that became grantable on 9 October
kql.why: graph-sp-seven-new-names-2026-10-09: the Microsoft Graph service principal gained seven names and two delegated scopes in the dump of 9 October 2026.
kql.desc: Lists every successful grant in the last 14 days of the two AppFederatedCredentialIssuers application roles and of the nine delegated scopes that arrived with them, with who granted it and to which service principal. An empty result is the expected one; a row for AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All needs an owner the same day. It needs Entra audit logs in a Log Analytics workspace, and the two modifiedProperties names it filters on should be confirmed against one known grant in your own tenant, because they are values in the log and not part of the published schema.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 10 Oct 2026 - grants of the Graph permissions that became grantable on 9 Oct 2026
// AuditLogs columns verified against the schema page cited beside this query.
// Role identifiers and scope names are read from the Microsoft Graph service principal dump of 9 Oct 2026.
let NewAppRoles = datatable(AppRoleId:string, Permission:string) [
  "231187a1-75b7-4554-a255-682d4d4971e8", "AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.Read.All",
  "aa595073-8ce6-409a-8b9e-258e9faab0f3", "AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All"
];
let NewScopes = dynamic([
  "AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.Read.All",
  "AppFederatedCredentialIssuers.ReadWrite.All",
  "CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.Read.All",
  "CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All",
  "CopilotCostManagement-Policy.Read.All",
  "CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All",
  "CopilotCostManagement-UserData.Read.All",
  "CrossTenantContentMigration.Read.All",
  "CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All"
]);
let AppGrants = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName == "Add app role assignment to service principal"
| where Result =~ "success"
| mv-expand Target = TargetResources
| mv-expand Prop = Target.modifiedProperties
| where tostring(Prop.displayName) == "AppRole.Id"
| extend AppRoleId = trim('"', tostring(Prop.newValue))
| join kind=inner NewAppRoles on AppRoleId
| extend GrantType = "Application";
let DelegatedGrants = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName == "Add delegated permission grant"
| where Result =~ "success"
| mv-expand Target = TargetResources
| mv-expand Prop = Target.modifiedProperties
| where tostring(Prop.displayName) == "DelegatedPermissionGrant.Scope"
| extend Scopes = split(trim(@'[" ]+', tostring(Prop.newValue)), " ")
| mv-expand Scope = Scopes to typeof(string)
| where Scope in (NewScopes)
| extend Permission = Scope, GrantType = "Delegated";
union AppGrants, DelegatedGrants
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)),
         GrantedTo = tostring(Target.displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, GrantType, Permission, GrantedTo, Actor, CorrelationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

kql.title: Who was granted an application role that deletes users' authentication methods
kql.why: graph-permref-33-documented-2026-10-08: Microsoft documented the thirteen delete-only authentication-method roles on 8 October 2026.
kql.desc: Lists every successful grant in the last 90 days of one of the thirteen application roles that delete users' authentication methods, with who granted it and to which service principal. The identifiers are the ones Microsoft's permissions reference printed on 8 October. An empty result is the expected one; any row outside a joiner-mover-leaver tool needs an owner. It needs Entra audit logs in a Log Analytics workspace, and the modifiedProperties layout should be confirmed on one known grant in your own tenant.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 9 Oct 2026 - grants of the authentication-method delete application roles
// AuditLogs columns verified against the schema page cited beside this query.
// The thirteen identifiers are the ones Microsoft's permissions reference printed on 8 Oct 2026.
let DeleteRoles = datatable(AppRoleId:string, Permission:string) [
  "712f5e0d-bc8d-4ae5-8242-cfb9a4921ed3", "UserAuthenticationMethod.Delete.All",
  "f0e9adfd-ed6b-45f5-b969-324a75286a39", "UserAuthMethod-Email.Delete.All",
  "7fa6d39e-1e4e-44be-bf9c-e8260b12e1f5", "UserAuthMethod-External.Delete.All",
  "9d8eb432-7ea3-491a-9ed7-e6361b308f08", "UserAuthMethod-HardwareOATH.Delete.All",
  "ae494ca6-9612-417a-972a-ef52efaf2de3", "UserAuthMethod-MicrosoftAuthApp.Delete.All",
  "9563fbd0-03a7-466e-8042-63d668b7d1a3", "UserAuthMethod-Passkey.Delete.All",
  "59f17651-8b6c-494e-a269-4ac582fbbca0", "UserAuthMethod-Phone.Delete.All",
  "bd760918-651f-4e67-b66f-8f614384dec2", "UserAuthMethod-PlatformCred.Delete.All",
  "e1c34213-26ac-400b-9548-a749f1b1a4e0", "UserAuthMethod-QR.Delete.All",
  "a71aecaf-82f1-47c5-ad0a-5e63503b928f", "UserAuthMethod-ResourceKey.Delete.All",

AuditLogs

| where tostring(Prop.displayName) == "AppRole.Id"
| extend AppRoleId = trim('"', tostring(Prop.newValue))

kql.title: Malicious URLs in Teams messages, with the QR-code-borne ones separated out
kql.why: MC1490905: Defender for Office 365 analyses URLs inside QR codes in Teams messages after delivery.
kql.desc: Defender for Office 365 now analyses URLs inside QR codes in Teams messages after delivery and, per Message Center, marks them with QRCode in a UrlLocation column of MessageUrlInfo. That column is not on the published schema page yet, so the query reads it through column_ifexists: before the rollout it lists every Teams URL with a threat verdict, and afterwards the QR-borne ones sort to the top. It needs Defender for Office 365 data in Advanced Hunting.

kql.title: Which applications still call the legacy Graph security alerts API, eight days before it stops answering
kql.desc: The legacy /security/alerts endpoint stops returning data after 15 October 2026, and a caller that is not migrated gets an empty answer rather than an error. This lists every application, service principal and user that called it in the last 14 days, with the call count and the last call; an empty result means nothing in the tenant depends on it. It needs Microsoft Graph activity logs in a Log Analytics workspace.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 7 Oct 2026 - which applications still call the legacy Graph security alerts API?
// Table and columns verified against the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs schema page cited beside this query.
// The legacy endpoint is /security/alerts; /security/alerts_v2 is its replacement and is excluded.
// Needs Microsoft Graph activity logs exported to a Log Analytics workspace (Entra diagnostic settings).
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RequestUri has "/security/alerts" and RequestUri !has "/security/alerts_v2"
| summarize Calls = count(),
            LastCall = max(TimeGenerated),
            Methods = make_set(RequestMethod, 5),
            StatusCodes = make_set(ResponseStatusCode, 10),
            SampleUri = take_any(RequestUri)
          by AppId, ServicePrincipalId, UserId, ApiVersion
| order by Calls desc

kql.title: Has any of the twelve newly grantable Graph application roles been assigned to a service principal
kql.why: graph-sp-twelve-new-names-2026-10-05: twelve application roles entered the Graph service principal between 29 September and 5 October.
kql.desc: Twelve application roles became grantable in the Microsoft Graph service principal between 29 September and 5 October, among them SynchronizationMetadata.ReadWrite.All and ContentHub-Installed.ReadWrite.All. This lists every app role assignment of one of the twelve role IDs in the last 14 days; an empty result is the expected one, and any row is a consent event to review. It needs Entra audit logs in a Log Analytics workspace. The property name inside modifiedProperties should be confirmed in your own tenant (inferred).
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 6 Oct 2026 - has any of the twelve newly grantable Graph application roles been assigned?
// Table and columns verified against the AuditLogs schema page cited beside this query.
// The role IDs are read from the Graph service principal dump of 5 October 2026, not typed.
// The property name AppRole.Id inside modifiedProperties is as Entra audit logs write it; confirm in your own tenant (inferred).
let NewRoleIds = dynamic([
    "71a8afcf-c9ac-4704-a49c-a2520ddfc6d8",
    "dc64b9ee-d7b6-4de6-97d3-189051d1c773",
    "9c668bfa-7e4d-4ea4-9f0b-ba2d67cac55c",
    "7090aa1b-99c0-444b-b40b-528bd2f35087",
    "0c6404f6-8e7a-413b-adc0-e9b750d959c8",
    "cc44d51e-040e-4631-a93a-1982ea54b428",
    "73fac914-e726-4af5-9a46-62f65f7b0a8b",
    "2ebdaf81-319a-4058-9cb1-7c2c20cda877",
    "7eb97e53-a7bc-4492-9113-1cd84a1ef8d8",
    "19f10513-d519-42cf-b01a-b3b662f46b8f",
    "3bb529ad-d59a-499c-abe2-736f636068a5",
    "4d482dd7-21ae-4e2d-97f9-58cd926f5c5e"]);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)

| mv-expand Target = TargetResources
| mv-expand Prop = Target.modifiedProperties
| where tostring(Prop.displayName) == "AppRole.Id"
| extend RoleId = trim('"', tostring(Prop.newValue))
| where RoleId in (NewRoleIds)
| project TimeGenerated, RoleId, GrantedTo = tostring(Target.displayName), InitiatedBy, Result, CorrelationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

kql.title: Who sends or receives .msix and .msixbundle attachments, before Outlook starts blocking them in November
kql.why: MC1488841: from early November 2026 .msix and .msixbundle are added to BlockedFileTypes in every OWA mailbox policy.
kql.desc: From early November 2026 Outlook on the web and new Outlook block .msix and .msixbundle attachments in every OWA mailbox policy. This lists who exchanged such attachments in the last 30 days, with file names and hashes, so that a business process that depends on them is found before the block and anything else is looked at as a delivery attempt.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 6 Oct 2026 - who sends or receives .msix and .msixbundle attachments before Outlook blocks them (MC1488841)
// Table and columns verified against the EmailAttachmentInfo schema page cited beside this query.
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".msix" or FileName endswith ".msixbundle"
| summarize Messages = dcount(NetworkMessageId), Files = make_set(FileName, 20), Hashes = make_set(SHA256, 20), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress
| order by Messages desc

kql.title: Who edits email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List today, before Security Operator loses that access in November
kql.why: MC1486293: from early November 2026 the Entra Security Operator role no longer maps to Security settings in Defender for Office 365 Unified RBAC.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 3 Oct 2026 - who changes MDO threat policies and Tenant Allow/Block List entries
// Columns verified against the CloudAppEvents schema page cited beside this query.
// ActionType values are Exchange Online cmdlet names; confirm them in your own tenant (inferred).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType has_any ("TenantAllowBlockListItems", "AntiPhishPolicy", "AntiPhishRule",
        "HostedContentFilterPolicy", "MalwareFilterPolicy", "SafeLinksPolicy", "SafeAttachmentPolicy")
| where ActionType startswith "New-" or ActionType startswith "Set-" or ActionType startswith "Remove-"
| summarize Changes = count(), Cmdlets = make_set(ActionType, 20), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId
| order by Changes desc

kql.title: Conditional Access policies that granted access on an unmanaged device claiming a mobile or macOS platform
kql.why: The device platform condition is unverified and spoofable through the user agent (Microsoft Learn, Conditional Access: Conditions).
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 30 Sep 2026 - platform-only Conditional Access grants on unmanaged devices
// Columns verified against the SigninLogs schema page cited beside this query.
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ResultType == "0"
| extend OS = tostring(DeviceDetail.operatingSystem),
         Managed = tostring(DeviceDetail.isManaged),
         Compliant = tostring(DeviceDetail.isCompliant)
| where OS has_any ("iOS", "Android", "MacOs", "Linux")
| where Managed != "true" and Compliant != "true"
| mv-expand CAP = ConditionalAccessPolicies
| where tostring(CAP.result) == "success"
| summarize SignIns = count(), Users = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
            Agents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 5)
            by Policy = tostring(CAP.displayName), OS
| order by SignIns desc

kql.title: Machine accounts that lost their domain trust after the 14 September out-of-band update
kql.why: The out-of-band update KB5129195 and KB5129194 carry a documented known issue: a domain-joined machine protected by Credential Guard can lose its Active Directory trust relationship because Machine Identity Isolation is now enforced. A host in that state stops satisfying device-based Conditional Access, so it looks like a compliance drift rather than a servicing fault. This query separates the two by pairing the update event with the trust failure on the same device.

kql.title: Service principal sign-ins with no interactive user, grouped the way Storm-3168 works
kql.why: The Storm-3168 write-up describes agentic tooling driving compromised service principals for cloud reconnaissance and credential access. A workload identity has no MFA and no sign-in risk, so the only signal is shape: a principal that suddenly reads far more than it used to, from an address range it has never used. This query gives the baseline and the break in one pass.

kql.title: Active Directory objects created by the Cloud Sync provisioning agent
kql.why: The 24 September preview lets Cloud Sync create users and groups inside on-premises AD DS. Until a rule knows which account does that, every one of those creations looks like an on-premises actor making directory objects. This query names the creator so the expected source can be excluded and everything else kept.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief 28 Sep 2026 - who creates objects in AD now that Cloud Sync can
// Table and columns verified against the IdentityDirectoryEvents schema page cited beside this query.
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("User created", "Group created", "Computer created")
| extend Target = tostring(TargetAccountUpn), Actor = tostring(AccountUpn)
| summarize Created = count(), Objects = make_set(Target, 100), Kinds = make_set(ActionType, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by Actor, DestinationDeviceName
| order by Created desc

pages.name: What are Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans? (preview)

add: # What are Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans? (preview)

Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans group related rules under shared assignments and conditions. Administrators can define common targeting and exclusions once, then configure each rule for a specific scenario. Use a plan to organize related controls around a security objective, such as requiring compliant devices or securing agent activity.

> Conditional Access policy plans are in preview. Preview features are available under the [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) and might not have all the capabilities of generally available features.

An organization might maintain separate Conditional Access policies for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android when each platform requires different settings. Those policies can repeat the same user targeting and emergency access exclusions. Changes to that shared targeting must then be made in each policy.

With a plan, shared targeting is defined once and automatically applies to every scenario within that plan. Adding or removing an emergency access group in one place updates the shared targeting for all rules in the plan.

Emergency access accounts, trusted service accounts, and privileged workstations appear in exclusion lists across many policies. Missed exclusions are a common source of unintended lockouts. Plans let administrators define these exclusions once, at the plan level, so no individual rule can accidentally omit them.

Organizations that deploy Global Secure Access often need hundreds of network-scoped rules that target the same user population and application set. Plans allow the shared targeting to be defined once, with each rule focused only on the specific network scope it governs.
### Apply consistent controls to agent activity

Agent identities can act with their own permissions or on behalf of a user by using the user's permissions. A plan can define a shared condition, such as high agent risk, and use separate rules to protect agent users and autonomous agents. Without a plan, each scenario requires a standalone policy that repeats the shared condition.

- **Plan details**: Specify a name, description, optional tags, and individual or group owners. These details help teams understand the plan's purpose, accountability, and the potential impact of future changes. Designating owners doesn't affect who has permission to edit the plan, and plan details don't affect policy enforcement at runtime.

- **Shared conditions**: Define optional include and exclude targeting that applies broadly. Shared conditions can include identities; resources such as applications; user actions; authentication context; risk levels; device platforms; network locations; and client app types.

- **Rules**: Define the individual enforcement scenarios within the plan. Each rule adds the assignments and conditions that are specific to the scenario, along with its grant and session controls. Every policy plan must have at least one rule.
> Select **All resources** at the rule level. This assignment isn't available in shared conditions.
Shared conditions and rule conditions combine additively:

- **Targeting at the plan level is inherited.** If the plan targets group A, every rule in the plan inherits that scope. A rule can't narrow the plan's targeting, but it can add exclusions of its own. For this reason, you can target **All users** in rules but not in shared conditions.

- **Identity type must be consistent.** Shared conditions can't mix identity types. A plan that targets users can't also target agents at the plan level. To cover multiple identity types in one plan, leave the identity assignment to the rules. For example, one rule can target users and another can target agents.

- **Inclusions and exclusions accumulate.** If the plan excludes emergency access groups A and B, and a rule also excludes group C, the effective exclusion list is A, B, and C. An exclusion set at the plan level can never be overridden or removed by a rule. This design ensures consistency across every rule in the plan.

At sign-in time, Conditional Access combines a rule's conditions with the plan's shared conditions, if any, to form the complete targeting for that rule. Each rule is then evaluated as an independent enforcement decision in the same way as a standalone policy. Each rule appears separately in sign-in logs.

> During preview, policy plans that target users with Location as a condition will be issued one-hour access tokens without instant IP enforcement check. For more information, see [Named location limitations](concept-continuous-access-evaluation.md#named-location-limitations).
## Relationship to existing Conditional Access policies
Plans are an addition to the existing Conditional Access policy model, not a replacement. Your existing policies continue to work as they do today, with no changes required.

During sign-in evaluation, the Conditional Access engine evaluates both existing policies and policy plan rules. Every applicable policy and every applicable rule must be satisfied for access to be granted. There's no interaction or precedence between them. They accumulate independently.
| Capability | Existing policy | Policy plans and rules |
| Targeting | Defined per policy and duplicated across policies | Shared conditions are defined once at the plan level and inherited by all rules, or defined per rule |
| Change management | Each policy is updated individually | A single change to the plan's shared conditions propagates to all rules |
| Policy templates | One template per policy | Combine multiple templates into a single plan, or deploy one template per plan |
To create, modify, or delete a policy plan, sign in with the Conditional Access Administrator role.

add: Microsoft Entra Kerberos trust configures the incoming trust-based flow by creating a Trusted Domain Object (TDO) in on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) for the Microsoft Entra Kerberos realm, `KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM`. The trust is inbound from the AD DS domain's perspective: Microsoft Entra ID trusts AD-issued cross-realm referral tickets for this realm. AD-authenticated clients can use these referral tickets to obtain Kerberos service tickets from Microsoft Entra ID for resources such as Azure Files and Azure SQL Managed Instance.
rem: Microsoft Entra Kerberos trust establishes an inbound trust relationship in which on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) trusts Microsoft Entra ID as a Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC). This trust enables hybrid identity organizations to use modern credentials for applications and allows Microsoft Entra ID to become the trusted source for cloud and on-premises authentication.

add: > The Trusted Domain Object isn't required for Windows Hello for Business cloud Kerberos trust or for passwordless security key (FIDO2) sign-in to on-premises resources. Those scenarios need only the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object, which you create with `Set-AzureADKerberosServer` without the `-SetupCloudTrust` parameter. For more information, see [Enable passwordless security key sign-in to on-premises resources](howto-authentication-passwordless-security-key-on-premises.md).

Use the Azure AD Hybrid Authentication Management PowerShell module to create a Trusted Domain Object in the AD DS domain and register trust information with Microsoft Entra ID. This creates an inbound trust from the AD DS domain's perspective, enabling Microsoft Entra ID to trust on-premises AD DS.
rem: Use the Azure AD Hybrid Authentication Management PowerShell module to set up a Trusted Domain Object in the Active Directory domain and register trust information with Microsoft Entra ID. This action creates an inbound trust relationship, which enables on-premises Active Directory to trust Microsoft Entra ID.

add: - Detect use of vulnerable SAP BTP custom apps (Preview)
### Detect use of vulnerable SAP BTP custom apps (Preview)

The SAP BTP solution adds an analytics rule that correlates SAP Application Vulnerability Report findings with BTP audit logs to detect use of custom apps with open high or critical vulnerabilities. The rule identifies interactive XSUAA logins that match a vulnerable app and application audit events in the same subaccount, Cloud Foundry organization, and space. It uses a default CVSS threshold of 7.0 and a 14-day finding lookback. For details, see [SAP BTP security content](sap/sap-btp-security-content#sap-application-vulnerability-report-service-preview).

| October 20, 2026 | Public preview | Cloud security plan management in the Defender portal |

The new Defender server security experience expands to include onboarding guidance for Azure and on-premises servers, building on the investigation and access management capabilities released on October 6.
- Onboard supported Azure virtual machines and Azure Arc-enabled servers automatically through Defender for Servers.
- Choose a supported deployment method to onboard Windows and Linux servers manually to Defender for Endpoint.
- Connect on-premises servers to Defender for Servers by using Azure Arc or Direct onboarding.
- Verify server onboarding and review available offboarding methods.
Servers already running Defender for Endpoint don't require reinstallation or migration to maintain their existing protection.
### Cloud security plan management in the Defender portal
Cloud security plan management is scheduled to become available in public preview in the Microsoft Defender portal for Azure commercial environments on October 20, 2026.
- Connect Azure subscriptions and management groups to cloud security in the Defender portal.
- Enable and manage cloud security plans globally across connected environments or configure plans for selected management groups and subscriptions.
- Estimate and track Cloud security costs, including cost under the new billing model, where usage is measured in Defender Workload Units (DWUs).
- Start a 30-day free trial for eligible cloud security plans when enabling plans.

When plan management moves to the Defender portal, plan configuration will be managed in the Defender portal and become view-only in the Azure portal. Migrated subscriptions will use DWU-based billing.
For more information, see [Microsoft Defender for Cloud in the Microsoft Defender portal](defender-portal/defender-for-cloud-defender-portal).

add: ### If you believe Microsoft disabled an application in error

Tenant administrators can't reverse Microsoft disablement by setting the service principal's `accountEnabled` property to `true` or by reactivating the app registration (`isDisabled=false`). This restriction also applies to administrators in the application's home tenant.

If your organization publishes the application, work with an administrator in its home tenant to contact Microsoft Support through the [general Microsoft Entra support options](~/fundamentals/how-to-get-support.md#open-a-support-request). Explain why you believe the disablement is an error, and include the application (client) ID, home tenant ID, `disabledByMicrosoftStatus` value, and relevant investigation findings. Opening a support request doesn't guarantee reactivation.

If your organization uses an application published by another organization, contact the publisher about the disablement and continue investigating the application's activity in your tenant. You can also use the general support options to get help with the impact on your tenant. Changing your tenant's sign-in setting doesn't remove the Microsoft disablement.

add: [![Diagram that shows the Platform SSO device and user registration sequence.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-02-registration.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-02-registration.png#lightbox)
*Figure 2. Device registration establishes device trust; user registration associates a user and authentication method with the Mac.*
The authentication method determines how the user proves their identity.
With the Password method, macOS synchronizes the local account password with the user's Microsoft Entra password:
1. After Platform SSO user registration completes, macOS Platform SSO (Apple) prompts the user to enter their Microsoft Entra password.
2. macOS uses the user's Microsoft Entra username and password to request a Platform SSO PRT. The request also includes device proof that binds it to the registered Mac.
3. Microsoft Entra ID verifies the credential, validates the device proof and issues the PRT.
4. After the PRT is issued successfully, macOS updates the local account password to match the Microsoft Entra password.
5. If the Microsoft Entra password changes later, macOS prompts the user to authenticate and updates the local password to keep the passwords synchronized.
This method reduces the number of passwords the user must manage, but it isn't passwordless or phishing-resistant
1. macOS Platform SSO (Apple) generates a user key protected by the Secure Enclave.
2. The user completes Microsoft Entra authentication and any additional authentication required to register the key.
3. The public key is registered with Microsoft Entra ID and associated with the user and registered Mac.
4. The private key remains protected by the Secure Enclave and isn't exported from the Mac.
5. The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in completes the user's Platform SSO configuration.

6. When requesting a Platform SSO PRT, macOS creates an assertion and signs it with the Secure Enclave-protected private key. The request also includes device proof that binds it to the registered Mac.
7. Microsoft Entra ID verifies the assertion with the registered public key, validates the user and device proofs, and issues the PRT.
rem: 1. The user completes Microsoft Entra authentication and any required multifactor authentication.
2. macOS creates or accesses a user key protected by the Secure Enclave.
3. The public key is registered with Microsoft Entra ID and associated with the user and device.
4. The private key remains protected on the Mac.
5. The extension completes the user's PSSO configuration.

add: The local account password remains a separate local credential and is never updated as part of PSSO with this auth method. Microsoft recommends  UserSecureEnclaveKey  for most Platform SSO deployments.
With the Smart Card method, the user proves their identity by using a certificate and its associated private key:
1. The user completes the required smart card and PIN interaction.
2. macOS creates an authentication assertion and uses the smart card's private key to sign it. The private key remains on the smart card and isn't exported.
3. The PRT request includes the signed assertion, the associated certificate information, and device proof that binds the request to the registered Mac.
4. Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication validates the certificate, user mapping, signed assertion, and device proof before Microsoft Entra ID issues the Platform SSO PRT.

## Authentication methods
The authentication method changes how the user proves identity. It doesn't change the broader device-registration and app-SSO architecture.
### Password

The Microsoft Entra password and local macOS password are synchronized according to PSSO policy. The authentication request remains bound to the registered Mac. This method reduces the number of passwords the user manages, but it isn't passwordless or phishing-resistant.
### UserSecureEnclaveKey

A hardware-bound user key is protected by the Secure Enclave. When fresh proof is required, macOS requests a signature from the private key and Microsoft Entra ID verifies it with the registered public key. The private key doesn't leave the Mac. The local account password remains a separate local credential.

2. The SSO plug-in supplies macOS Platform SSO (Apple) with Kerberos ticket mappings that identify the cloud and on-premises TGT fields in the Microsoft Entra response.

3. macOS Platform SSO (Apple) sends a Platform SSO PRT request to Microsoft Entra ID. Based on the configuration supplied by the SSO plug-in, the request indicates that available Kerberos TGTs should be returned alongside the PRT in the same protected response.

4. Microsoft Entra ID verifies the registered credential and validates the user and device proofs. It then returns the Platform SSO PRT and any available cloud or on-premises TGTs in the protected response.
5. macOS Platform SSO (Apple) decrypts and validates the response.

6. Based on the configured TGT mappings, macOS imports the selected TGTs into a Kerberos credential cache. If **custom_tgt_setting**  isn't specified, the SSO plug-in maps both the cloud and on-premises TGTs by default. Administrators can configure it to map both TGTs, only the cloud TGT, only the on-premises TGT, or neither TGT.

7. If the Kerberos SSO extension is configured with **usePlatformSSOTGT** enabled, macOS makes Platform SSO TGT available to the extension when the ticket’s realm matches the realm requested by the extension.

8. The Kerberos SSO extension uses the matching TGT to obtain service tickets for cloud or on-premises Kerberos resources without prompting the user to authenticate again, provided that the TGT remains valid and the resource configuration permits SSO.

add: - The Microsoft Defender Antivirus threat severity represents the absolute severity of the detected threat (malware). It's assigned based on the potential risk to the individual device, if infected.
- The Defender for Endpoint alert severity represents the severity of the detected behavior, which is the actual risk to the device but more importantly the potential risk to the organization.

- The severity of a Defender for Endpoint alert about a Microsoft Defender Antivirus detected threat that was prevented and did not infect the device is categorized as *Informational* because there was no actual damage.

- Commercial malware that is detected while running but blocked and remediated by Microsoft Defender Antivirus generates a *Low* alert because it might have caused some damage to the individual device but poses no organizational threat.

- Malware that is detected while running and can pose a threat both to the individual device and to the organization might be ranked as *Medium* or *High*, regardless of whether it is eventually blocked.
rem: The Microsoft Defender Antivirus threat severity represents the absolute severity of the detected threat (malware), and is assigned based on the potential risk to the individual device, if infected.
The Defender for Endpoint alert severity represents the severity of the detected behavior, the actual risk to the device but more importantly the potential risk to the organization.
So, for example:

- The severity of a Defender for Endpoint alert about a Microsoft Defender Antivirus detected threat that was prevented and did not infect the device is categorized as "Informational" because there was no actual damage.

- An alert about a commercial malware was detected while executing, but blocked and remediated by Microsoft Defender Antivirus, is categorized as "Low" because it may have caused some damage to the individual device but poses no organizational threat.

- An alert about malware detected while executing which can pose a threat not only to the individual device but to the organization, regardless if it was eventually blocked, may be ranked as "Medium" or "High".

### Will my Defender for Identity v3.x sensor continue working if I offboard the server from Defender for Endpoint?

No. Offboarding a server from Defender for Endpoint stops Defender for Identity v3.x sensor reporting, including sensors migrated from v2.x. Offboarding doesn't automatically switch the server to identity-only mode.

To deploy sensor v3.x without full Defender for Endpoint protection, use [onboarding without Defender for Endpoint deployment](deploy/activate-sensor#onboard-a-domain-controller-without-defender-for-endpoint-deployment).

add: # Customer intent: As an IT admin, I want to investigate autonomous agent sign-in failures and identify affected applications so that I can restore intended agent access without weakening security controls.
# How to investigate Agent ID autonomous sign-ins

Microsoft Entra Health Monitoring provides tenant-level health signals and alerts when it detects a significant change in your tenant's activity. The **Agent ID autonomous sign-ins** scenario helps you investigate failures when agents authenticate and act as themselves.

The new page covers creating the Trusted Domain Object, client configuration, key rotation, and removing the object. On rotation: 'Microsoft doesn't mandate a fixed rotation interval. Rotate the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server key on the same schedule as other Active Directory Kerberos (krbtgt) keys, during scheduled security maintenance windows, and immediately after a suspected credential compromise.' And: 'Other tools can rotate krbtgt keys, but you must use the Set-AzureADKerberosServer cmdlet for the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server.'
entries.after: Revised 21 October 2026 (commit 42c3495, ms.date 10/19/2026): the page no longer says on-premises AD DS trusts Microsoft Entra ID. It now states the procedure creates a Trusted Domain Object in AD DS for the realm KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM, inbound from the AD DS domain's perspective, so Microsoft Entra ID trusts AD-issued cross-realm referral tickets, which AD-authenticated clients use to get service tickets from Entra ID for Azure Files and Azure SQL Managed Instance. New note: the Trusted Domain Object is not required for Windows Hello for Business cloud Kerberos trust or FIDO2 sign-in to on-premises resources, which need only the Kerberos server object (Set-AzureADKerberosServer without -SetupCloudTrust).

entries.after: Microsoft Entra blog, 12 October 2026: 'The guided migration tool gives eligible organizations a structured path from Microsoft Entra Connect Sync to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync', covering readiness assessment, provisioning agent and Cloud Sync configuration, activation through a controlled transition and post-activation validation. roles.impact: The role this catalog has carried since 25 August as live-but-undocumented is now published. Microsoft's four actions are disable a user, enable a user, invalidate all refresh tokens and update a password — enough to take over a non-privileged account, which is why two of them carry the PRIVILEGED label. The role header carries the privileged label too, so it is in scope for PIM and for privileged-role access reviews.

roles.impact: A role widely handed out for reading and configuring security policy becomes able to disable an account, terminate its live sessions and force a credential reset. Nobody consents to it and no assignment changes; the capability simply arrives. It is the same capability Microsoft carved into the deliberately narrow SOC Identity Responder role in June 2026.
roles.action: Pull the current holders and treat the list as a new privileged role. Move standing assignments into PIM with approval and justification, drop holders who only ever needed to read policy, and alert on Disable account, Revoke sign-in sessions and Reset user password performed by a principal holding Security Administrator.

The date carried is Microsoft's, not this brief's: the edit is Microsoft's and it is dated 3 September.

graph.name: /beta/security/caseManagement/cases/*/attachments/*/content
graph.before: case evidence content could not be transferred over Graph, and relations and tasks could not be read individually or deleted
graph.after: chunked upload and post-malware-scan download of attachment content, plus GET and DELETE on relations and DELETE on tasks
graph.impact: An app with CaseManagement.ReadWrite.All can exfiltrate raw investigation evidence and destroy the links and tasks that record an investigation's structure — evidence theft and anti-forensics against your own case management, from a single permission.
graph.action: Restrict CaseManagement.ReadWrite.All to named SOAR service principals and alert on DELETE against case relations and tasks.

graph.name: EntitlementManagement.ReadWrite.All → externalOriginResourceConnectors
graph.before: entitlement management had no connector to an external identity governance system
graph.after: create and manage connections to SAP IAG, carrying the SAP endpoint, OAuth token endpoint, client ID, and the Azure subscription, resource group, key vault and secret name holding its client secret
graph.impact: An existing, already-granted permission silently gained the ability to create an outbound trust and a Key Vault secret reference pointing at an external system. No new consent prompt fires, so an app approved months ago for access-package automation can now stand up a provisioning path into SAP.
graph.action: Enumerate /identityGovernance/entitlementManagement/externalOriginResourceConnectors and re-review every service principal holding EntitlementManagement.ReadWrite.All — its blast radius grew without a consent event.

graph.name: accessReviewReviewerScope → reviewerId, scopeType
graph.consent: Not stated by Microsoft — permissions on the access review APIs are unchanged
graph.before: a reviewer could only be designated through a query expression; principal and resource scoping likewise required a query
graph.after: reviewerId names a reviewer directly by ID, and scopeType selects a well-known scope via new enumerations
graph.impact: Designating the reviewer of a privileged access review is now a single ID field rather than a query an auditor would have to parse, which makes it materially easier for a principal with access-review write rights to install itself or a chosen account as reviewer and rubber-stamp continued privileged access.
graph.action: Re-read reviewerId on your Global Administrator and privileged-role access review definitions and confirm the reviewer is who you expect.

graph.name: /beta/me/distributionLists/{id} → members
graph.before: standalone methods existed for listing and getting distribution list members
graph.after: those methods are removed. members is now a read-only expandable relationship, not returned by default
graph.impact: Any tooling that enumerates distribution list membership for recipient or data-flow auditing breaks silently, returning an empty members collection rather than an error when $expand is not supplied.
graph.action: Update DL-membership collection scripts to use ?$expand=members and verify they are not now reporting empty membership.

graph.name: ThreatHunting.Read.All
graph.before: Run hunting queries — advanced hunting only, no access to stored query objects
graph.after: Run hunting queries and read saved hunting queries — plus GET /security/threathunting/queries and GET /security/threathunting/queries/{id}
graph.impact: Saved hunting queries are detection logic. Any application already consented to ThreatHunting.Read.All — typically a SOAR connector or a reporting job — can now enumerate the whole saved-query library without a new consent prompt, which means the team's coverage and its blind spots are readable by anything that could already run a hunt.
graph.action: List every service principal holding ThreatHunting.Read.All and decide, per app, whether reading the saved query library is in scope. Add GET /security/threathunting/queries to the set of Graph calls worth auditing.
