graph.name: User.ReadBasic.All
graph.consent: Application: admin consent required · Delegated: not required
graph.before: returns a basic set of profile properties and, per Microsoft, also app role assignments and license details — behaviour Microsoft describes as accidental
graph.after: returns the basic profile properties only. App role assignments move to User.Read.All and license details to LicenseAssignment.Read.All
graph.impact: Two effects at once. Applications that quietly relied on the extra data break with no deprecation window — Microsoft states no sunset date. And a low-consent scope (delegated User.ReadBasic.All needs no admin consent) stops exposing licence and app-assignment data, which is reconnaissance material for anyone mapping who holds which application role.
graph.action: List service principals granted User.ReadBasic.All and check which of them read app role assignments or licence data. Applications that legitimately need it must be re-consented to User.Read.All or LicenseAssignment.Read.All, both of which require admin consent — so this is a consent-review task, not a code change.

displayText.Application: Read all users' basic profiles
displayText.Delegated: Read all users' basic profiles

descriptionByType.Application: Allows the app to read a basic set of profile properties of other users in your organization without a signed-in user. Includes display name, first and last name, email address, open extensions, and photo.
descriptionByType.Delegated: Allows the app to read a basic set of profile properties of other users in your organization on behalf of the signed-in user. This includes display name, first and last name, email address and photo.

history.note: Entered the catalog with the permission inventory baseline, parsed from Microsoft’s permissions reference.

Microsoft announced on 1 September 2026 that the permission “accidentally allows the app to read app role assignments and license details of users” and that this access is being removed. The permissions reference already describes only the basic profile properties, so the documentation does not move — the service does.

Microsoft published MC1470871 on 11 September 2026, giving the change its rollout window: general availability worldwide from mid-September 2026, expected complete by late September. The post names the replacement permissions — User.Read.All for app role assignments, LicenseAssignment.Read.All for licence details — and states the reason as a security vulnerability. The catalog entry moves from an announcement with no date to a change already rolling.

graph.dateNote: 1 September 2026 is Microsoft's own publication date for the announcement. No retirement or enforcement date is stated by Microsoft.

graph.impact: An application holding this can delete a user's registered authentication methods without a signed-in user. graph.name: Group.Read.All → onPremisesExtensionAttributes

descriptionByType.Reach: Microsoft added the onPremisesExtensionAttributes property to the group resource on v1.0. extensionAttribute1 through extensionAttribute15, synchronised from on-premises Active Directory, are now readable on groups.

graph.socNote: No consent prompt fires. Every application already holding Group.Read.All or Group.ReadWrite.All starts seeing on-premises extension attributes on groups it could already read. Those attributes routinely carry cost centre, business unit and classification values, and organisations use them as dynamic membership rule inputs. Re-read what your group-reading applications are entitled to see.

graph.name: AgentIdentityBlueprint.ReadWrite.All → isDisabled

descriptionByType.Reach: Microsoft added the isDisabled property to agentIdentityBlueprint on beta, so an agent identity blueprint can be deactivated without being deleted.

graph.socNote: A kill switch for an agent identity that leaves the object in place. Worth wiring into the agent offboarding runbook now, while the surface is still small: disabling beats deleting when an agent has to be stopped during an investigation and its history has to survive.

descriptionByType.delegated: Grants the application the same access to Dataverse and Dynamics 365 model-driven apps as the signed-in user has, for the environment named in the scope.
